name: Modifier
description:
Modifiers are values that influence how the game works, by for example adding or multiplying to a certain calculation.
Modifiers are attached to a certain entity, such as [country_modifiers|e] to [countries|e], [location_modifiers|e] to [locations|e], [character_modifiers|e] to [characters|e] and [international_organization_modifiers|e] to [international_organizations|e].

name: Location Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to a [location|e].

name: Province Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to a [province|e].

name: Country Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to an entire [country|e].

name: Unit Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to a particular [unit|e].

name: Character Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to the [character|e]. Modifier types which are supposed to target the [country|e] are only active if the character is the [ruler|e] of that country.

name: Dynasty Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to the [dynasty|e]. Modifier types which are supposed to target the [character|e] are active on every living member of the dynasty, though [country_modifiers|e] are only applied if the character is the [ruler|e] of that country.

name: Movement Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to the [movement|e]. These will apply to each [location|e] a movement affects.

name: Decaying Modifier
description: Decaying Modifiers are like regular [modifiers|e], but their effects gradually weaken as they near their expiration date. This creates temporary changes that fade over time.

name: International Organization Modifier
description: A [modifier|e] that applies to the [international_organization|e].

name: Effect
description: Effects are used in order to affect the game dynamically. They can range from the simple addition of [gold|e] to more complex actions like the unlocking of a [government_reform|e]. Effects usually happen in an [event|e] or are the rewards from [missions|e].

name: Trigger
description: Triggers are conditions which need to be fulfilled in order for certain [effects|e], [events|e], [tasks|e] and other kind of game elements to be active.

name: Action
description: An action is a button which causes an [effect|e] in the game world. Such actions are usually in the form of [country_interactions|e], [situation_actions|e] or [unit_abilities|e].

name: Tithe
description: This is the amount of [gold|e] collected from all [pops|e] of the [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] faith in countries following the same faith, and given to the Papacy. Countries with negative [opinion|e] of the Papacy will not pay the tithe.

name: Curia
description: The Curia is the administrative body of the Holy See and therefore of the [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] Church itself. Any [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] [country|e] can interact with the Curia and spend [religious_influence|e] to propose a [curia_action|e].

name: Overseas
description: This is a [location|e] that has no land connection to the [capital|e] of a [country|e], is on another [continent|e], and is not on an adjacent [sub_continent|e].

name: Fertility
description: This impacts the ability of a [character|e] becoming pregnant if they are female, or to get a female pregnant when they are a male.

name: Goods Demand
description: These are the [goods|e] that are required for a [construction|e], a [production_method|e], [pop_needs|e] or anything else that requires goods.

name: Reformation
description:
The $game_concept_reformation$ is an influential movement within the [ShowReligionGroupAdjective('christian')] World which fragments the [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] faith into several other religions. This movement starts with [ShowSituationName('reformation')] [situation|e].
The following religions are part of the $game_concept_reformation$:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowReligionName('hussite')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowReligionName('lutheran')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowReligionName('calvinist')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowReligionName('anglican')]

name: Reform Desire
description: [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] religion has internal conflicts between what is the correct doctrine or not, and about what is part of the faith or not. As time goes by, the desire to reform becomes bigger, and will impact any future discussion about the doctrine of [ShowReligionNameWithNoTooltip('catholic')].

name: War Allies
description: These are [countries|e] that are helping each other on the same side of a [war|e].

name: Country
description:
A Country is a political entity that can participate in [diplomacy|e]. It has a [government|E], a [primary_culture|e], and a [primary_religion|e]. It may control [armies|e] and [navies|e] to project its power.

Every Country is either [settled|E], [extraterritorial|E], [army_based|e], or a [society_of_pops|E].

Each Country is played either by a human player or by an AI.

name: Ruler
description:
Every [country|E] may have a [character|E] as its ruler. Depending on the [government_type|e] they may rule for life, or for a set period of time, before being replaced. The [traits|E] of a ruler affect the entire [country|e], and the [adm|e], [mil|e], and [dip|e] have a direct impact on the efficiency of the [cabinet|e].

Future rulers are selected by the [heir_selection|e]. While there is no legitimate [adult], the [government] is instead ruled by a [regent|e].

name: Title History
description: The $game_concept_title_history$ is the relation of all the [countries|e] that a [character|e] has ruled during their lives.

name: Formable Country
description:
A Formable Country is a new national identity that can be formed (or re-formed) by a [country|e] fulfilling certain conditions.

These conditions might include controlling a percentage of the [locations|e] in a [region|e], or having a specific [primary_culture|e].

We can only form a Formable Country that has a higher [tier|e] than our current [tier].

Typically, they represent historical unions, or even legendary ambitions. Upon formation, the old [country] will change its name, flag, and colors to that of the Formable Country.

name: Settled Country
description: A $game_concept_settled_country$ is a [country|e] that needs to [own|e] [locations|e] in order to exist.

name: Extraterritorial Country
description: An $game_concept_extraterritorial_country$ is a [country|e] that exists by virtue of its [buildings|e], and does not need to [own|e] entire [locations|e].

name: Society of Pops
description: A $game_concept_society_of_pops$ is a [country|e] that exists by virtue of its [pops|e], and does not need to [own|e] entire [locations|e].

name: Army Based Country
description: An $game_concept_army_based$ is a [country|e] that can [own|e] [locations|e], but its existence is relying entirely on its [armies|e]. If those are destroyed, then the $game_concept_country$ collapses.

name: Navy Based Country
description: A $game_concept_navy_based$ is a [country|e] that can [own|e] [locations|e], but its existence is relying entirely on its [navies|e]. If those are destroyed, then the $game_concept_country$ collapses.

name: Regency
description:
A Regency occurs while a [government|e] has no legitimate [ruler|e], and is instead led by a [regent|e].

Usually it is caused when the [heir_selection|e] produces no valid [heir|e], or when the [heir] is a mere [child|e].

In a [ShowGovernmentTypeName('monarchy')], the [consort|e] may become the [regent], but otherwise it is a [character|e] associated with the most powerful [estate|e], or even the [overlord|e].

The Regency persists until a proper [ruler] is restored.

name: Province Capital
description:
The Province Capital is the [location|e] that is the figurative heart of its [province|e]. The most populated or developed [location] in a [province] will be automatically selected as the Province Capital, although it can be manually changed from the Location Panel. When this [location] gets [occupied|e] during a [war|e], the remaining [locations] of the [province] fall automatically in the hands of the invader over a short period of time.

The Province Capital also determines the [market|e] from which the whole [province|e] buys and sells [food|e].

name: Province
description: A province is a group of [locations|e] [owned|e] by the same [country|e]. The province shares and distributes [food|e] between its locations, and [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e] are raised from an entire province at once. Several [cabinet_actions|e] target a province.

name: Province Definition
description:
A Province Definition is a predetermined group of [locations|e] that determines how [provinces|e] are created throughout the game.

[areas_with_icon|e] are divided into Province Definitions, which in turn contain [locations_with_icon|e]. All [locations] in the same Province Definition that are [owned|e] by the same [country_with_icon|e] will belong to the same [province|e].

If multiple [countries] [own] [locations] in the same Province Definition, there will be as many different [provinces], each with its own [province_capital_with_icon|e] and [food_stockpile_with_icon|e].

name: Geography
description: Geography is the nature and relative arrangement of places and physical features. [continents|e], [sub_continents|e], [regions|e], [areas|e], [provinces|e] and [locations|e] are all parts of the world's geography.

name: Geographical Term
description: An arbitrary collection of geographical concepts like [continents|e], [sub_continents|e], [regions|e], [areas|e], [provinces|e] and [locations|e].

name: Continent
description: The world is divided into a few continents, and these continents are then divided into [sub_continents|e].

name: Subcontinent
description: A Subcontinent is a group of [regions|e] that is part of a [continent|e]. [ShowSubContinentName('western_europe')] or $india$ are examples of a Subcontinent.

name: Region
description: A Region is a group of [areas|e] that is part of a [sub_continent|e]. [ShowRegionName('scandinavian_region')] would be an example of a Region.

name: Area
description: An Area is a group of [provinces|e], and is part of a [region|e].

name: Port
description: A port is a land [location|e] next to the sea which has the potential to build and moor [ships|e].

name: Fortification
description:
These are defensive [buildings|e] designed to protect the [country|e]'s own [locations|e] against [enemy|e] [armies|e]. A [location] with a fort can not be [sieged|e] instantly, but instead will require a prolonged [siege]. Certain [advances|e] will allow the construction of more effective forts, with each level increasing the difficulty of the [siege] required to [occupy|e] them.

Forts have a [zone_of_control|e] over adjacent [locations].

Forts have [fort_maintenance_with_icon|e] costs that go directly to the Country's [treasury], and depend on the prices of [goods] in their [market|e]. All [countries] have a [fort_limit] to the number of forts they can maintain efficiently, and surpassing it increases the [fort_maintenance] considerably.

name: Fort Limit
description:
The $game_concept_fort_limit$ of a [country_with_icon|e] represents its ability to maintain its [fortifications_with_icon|e] without overburdening the administration. A [country] can surpass its Fort Limit, but doing so will incur progressively higher [fort_maintenance_with_icon|e] costs.

The $game_concept_fort_limit$ increases chiefly with the number of owned [locations_with_icon|e], but also with the [country_rank_with_icon|e] and the number of [locations] with [ShowLocationRankName('city')] [location_rank|e]. The [ShowSocietyDirectionName('defensive')] [societal_value_with_icon|e] and some [advances_with_icon|e] may also increase it.

name: Zone of Control
description:
It represents the defensive capabilities of a [fortification|e] to block the movement of [enemy|e] [armies|e] through the [locations|e] adjacent to it. An invading [army] standing on an [enemy] [location] adjacent to an [enemy] [fort] will have to [siege|e] the [fort] first before it can move past it to any other adjacent [location] of that [fort].

Friendly Zone of Control also shelters [armies] from local [attrition|e] sources, including [winter|e]. This shelter extends to forts owned by your direct [subjects|e] and to your direct [overlord|e].

name: Tax Rate
description: The percentage of the [max_tax|e] an [estate|e] pays as [taxes|e].

name: Max Tax
description: This is the largest percentage of [tax|e] that can be taken from an [estate|e].

name: Min Tax
description: This is the lowest percentage of [tax|e] that can be taken from an [estate|e].

name: Tax
description:
We can elect to collect taxes from our [estates|e]. This will increase our [treasury|e], but higher taxes will decrease their [estate_satisfaction|e].

The amount of [wealth|e] that can be taxed depends on the [control|e] of the [locations|e] generating [wealth] for the [estates].

name: Bankrupt
description:
A [country|e] choosing to go bankrupt will clear all its [debt|e]. However, this will bring a 5-year period of harsh [modifiers|e].
A [country] can also be forced into bankruptcy if it runs out of money while unable to take more [loans|e].

name: Economic Base
description:
This is based on the total [wealth|e] and [population|e] of a [country|e], regardless of [control|e].

The number of [subjects|e] and [institutions|e] embraced also increases it, as well as any [income|e] from [interest|e] or [foreign_buildings|e].

name: Profit
description:
This is the amount that a [building|e] or a [rgo|e] contributes to the [wealth|e] of its [location]. In other words, the [gold|e] that are created from the [building].

If it is negative, the building will be considered unprofitable and stop working.

name: Taxable Profit
description: This is the amount of [gold|e] created by a [building] or [rgo] that is affected by [taxes|e], taking [control|e] into account.

name: Tax Base
description:
The Tax Base is the total amount of [wealth|e] that can be affected by [taxes|e] in a [location], which directly depends on its [control|e]. Wealth without [control] goes directly to the [estates], and cannot be taxed.

[wealth] is divided among the [estates] according to their [wealth_share|e] in the [location]. Every [estate] then pays a portion of that Tax Base to the [treasury|e] according to the [tax_rate|e] imposed on them.

name: Wealth
description:
The Wealth of a [location|e] is the combined profit of its [rgo|e] and [buildings|e] from selling their [goods|e] to the [market|e]. If there are [ShowPopTypeName('burghers')] present in the [location], [burgher_trade|e] may also increase the Location Wealth.

The Wealth of a [location] is divided among the [estates|e] according to their [wealth_share] in the [location]. Location Wealth multiplied by [control|e] forms the [tax_base|e] of a [location], which is the [gold|e] that can be taxed by the government. Wealth without [control] goes directly to the [estates], and cannot be taxed.

name: Wealth Share
description:
The [wealth|e] of a [location|e] is distributed among the [estates|e] according to their relative [population|e] in the [location]. [ShowPopTypeName('nobles')] get a much bigger share per capita than [ShowPopTypeName('burghers')], which in turn get a much bigger share per capita than [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')].

Depending on the [ShowModifierTypeName('local_peasant_enfranchisment')] in a [location], a percentage of the share of the [ShowEstateTypeName('peasants_estate')] is transferred to the [ShowEstateTypeName('nobles_estate')].

name: Tax Efficiency
description: This is how efficient our [country|e] is at collecting [tax|e]. It affects the amount of $game_concept_taxes$ that reach the [treasury|e] when taxing the [estates|e].

name: Production Efficiency
description: This impacts the [output|e] of [buildings|e]. A positive Production Efficiency increases the profit, while a negative may make it not worth keeping open.

name: Establishment
description: Newly constructed [buildings|e] start unestablished. Below the establishment threshold, they operate at reduced throughput, both consuming fewer inputs and producing less output. Once the threshold is reached, the building operates at full capacity and begins earning a bonus to [production_efficiency|e] proportional to how established it is, growing up to +[GetDefine('NEconomy','STARTUP_MAX_PE_BONUS')|+=2%] at full establishment. [establishment|e] is gained each month and is lost if the building closes.

name: Selling Efficiency
description: This modifies how profitable a [trade|e] will be, by directly impacting the price you sell [goods|e] to the target [market|e].

name: Export Efficiency
description: This modifies how profitable a [trade|e] will be on the sell side, by directly impacting the price received when exporting [goods|e] to a foreign [market|e].

name: Import Efficiency
description: This reduces the cost paid when importing [goods|e] from a foreign [market|e].

name: Manpower
description:
Manpower represents the limit of how many blaggards and scoundrels a [country|e] can support in its standing [army|e].

Manpower is expended when training and maintaining professional [regiments|e], which are usually more effective than [army_levies|e].

The rate at which Manpower is gained can be increased by constructing Manpower [buildings|e] or researching certain [advances|e].

name: Sailors
description:
A [country|e] may possess a number of Sailors, representing the fishermen, merchant seamen, and naval officers who make a living on the open seas.

Such experienced tars are required to build [ships|e], and are expended while maintaining a [navy|e]. These are separate from [navy_levies|e] and more effective. They are even required to man [exploration|e] missions.

The rate at which Sailors are gained can be increased by constructing port [buildings|e] or researching certain [advances|e].

name: Religion
description:
A Religion is any system of beliefs that belongs to a [religion_group|e]. Every [person|e] has a Religion (and may be [converted|e] to a different one), and every [country|e] has a [primary_religion|e].

Religions in the same [religion_group] consider each other to be [heretic|e], while Religions in different [religion_groups] consider each other to be [heathen|e]. Additionally, Religions may have specific opinions about other Religions.

name: Dominant Religion
description:
The Dominant Religion is the [religion|e] with the most [pops|e] following it in a [location|e] or a [country|e].
This does not necessarily mean that it is the majority.

name: Dominant Country
description: The [country|e] that has the most [population|e] of their [primary_culture|e] becomes the [dominant_country|e] of that [culture|e]. A Country cannot be $game_concept_dominant_country_dominant$ if their [overlord|e] is of the same $game_concept_culture$.

name: Religion Group
description: A Religion Group is a set of [religions|e] that are similar, and may view each other as merely wrong instead of evil. This will not stop them from starting [wars|e] against each other.

name: Culture
description:
A Culture is a group of [people|e] who share a sense of kinship.

Each Culture possesses a [language|e], which it may share with other Cultures.

Each Culture has a [cultural_tradition|e], and a [cultural_influence|e]. Different Cultures have changing [cultural_opinions|e] of each other.

Each [country|e] has a [primary_culture|e], and may have several [accepted_cultures|e] and/or [tolerated_cultures|e] in addition. All other Cultures in the country are considered [non_accepted_cultures|e]. Cultures can be [assimilated|e] by other Cultures.

Many Cultures belong to one or more [culture_groups|e].

name: Graphical Culture
description: The main [culture|e] used for the representation of the in-game graphics and visuals.

name: Ethnicity
description: $game_concept_ethnicity$ is what defines the main physical features of a [character|e].

name: Culture Group
description:
A Culture Group is a set of [cultures|e] that are similar in some way, whether through shared heritage, similar traditions, or just regional proximity.

A [culture] may belong to any number of Culture Groups, though they may also be isolated enough to not belong to any.

[countries|e] whose [primary_cultures|e] share at least one Culture Group will have a small [opinion|e] bonus of each other, though it does not stack if they share multiple.

Some [culture_groups] can eventually be [merged_culture_group_merged|e].

name: Unified Culture Group
description:
Some [culture_groups|e] can be $game_concept_merged_culture_group_merged$ into a single [culture|e].

A country can $game_concept_merged_culture_group_merge$ one of their [primary_culture|e]'s [culture_groups], which will cause a new [culture] to be created. [pops|e] of the old [primary_culture|e] and those of [accepted_cultures|e] that are in the same [culture_group_short] and use the same [language|e] will be immediately assimilated.

$game_concept_merged_culture_groups$ have a significant bonus to [assimilating|e] Cultures of that $game_concept_culture_group$.

A [culture_group] can only be $game_concept_merged_culture_group_merged$ once.

name: Dominant Language
description:
The Dominant Language is the [language|e] with the most [pops|e] speaking it in a [location|e].
This does not necessarily mean that it is the majority.

name: Dominant Dialect
description:
The $game_concept_dominant_dialect$ is the [dialect|e] with the most [pops|e] speaking it in a [location|e].
This does not necessarily mean that it is the majority.

name: Dominant Culture
description:
The dominant culture is the largest [culture|e] in a [location|e] or a [country|e].
This does not necessarily mean that it is the majority.

name: Primary Culture
description:
This is the [culture|e] that a [country|E] is considered to belong to. [pops|e] of another culture will [assimilate|e] to this when the circumstances are right.

The [common_language|e] of each [country] is determined by the [language] of their Primary Culture.

[pops] belonging to the $game_concept_primary_culture$ of a [country] will see their [pop_satisfaction_with_icon|e] increased by [GetDefine('NPop','PRIMARY_CULTURE_SATISFACTION')|%G].

name: Primary or Accepted Culture
description: This is a [culture|e] that is either a [primary_culture_short|e] or [accepted_culture|e] in a [country|E].

name: Religious Status
description:
This is how a [religion|e] is categorized compared to [primary_religion|e].
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[primary_religion|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[heretic|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[heathen|e]

name: Primary Religion
description:
The official [religion|e] of a [country|e]. It gives access to different content and mechanics, and may allow for very different playstyles.

[pops|e] will have higher [pop_satisfaction|e] if they belong to the $game_concept_primary_religion$, and other $game_concept_pops$ will slowly [convert|e] to the $game_concept_primary_religion$ under the right conditions.

The $game_concept_primary_religion$ also has great impact on [diplomacy|e], since brethren $game_concept_countries$ tend to see each other in a more favorable light.

name: Cultural Capacity
description: The cost for a [country|e] to have a [culture|e] as an [accepted_culture|e] depends on their [cultural_opinion|e] of the [primary_culture|e] and the size of that culture in relation to the $game_concept_primary_culture$.

name: Accepted Culture
description:
Each [country|e] can have a handful of [cultures|e] that are treated entirely like the [primary_culture|e].

The exact amount of cultures a country can afford to accept without penalties is variable, and can be increased by some [advances|e].

[pops|e] belonging to an Accepted Culture can be raised as [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e] without requiring any special [law|e].

[pops_with_icon|e] belonging to an $game_concept_accepted_culture$ will see their [pop_satisfaction_with_icon|e] increased by [GetDefine('NPop','ACCEPTED_CULTURE_SATISFACTION')|%G].

name: Tolerated Culture
description:
Each [country|e] can have a handful of [cultures|e] that are treated better than [non_accepted_cultures|e] but not as good as [primary_culture|e].

The exact amount of cultures a country can afford to tolerate without penalties is variable, and can be increased by some [advances|e].

[pops|e] belonging to a Tolerated Culture can be raised as [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e] without requiring any special [law|e].

[pops_with_icon|e] belonging to an $game_concept_tolerated_culture$ will see their [pop_satisfaction_with_icon|e] increased by [GetDefine('NPop','TOLERATED_CULTURE_SATISFACTION')|%G].

name: Discriminated Culture
description:
Every [culture|e] present in a [country|e] that is neither the [primary_culture|e], nor an [accepted_culture|e], nor a [tolerated_culture|e] counts as a Discriminated Culture.

Pops belonging to such a [culture] may not be raised as [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e] without a special [law|e].

name: Foreign Culture
description: This is the [cultural_status|e] of a [culture|e] that has no [pops|e] at all inside the [country|e].

name: Cultural Status
description:
Every [culture|e] is viewed as one of these by a [country|e]:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[primary_culture|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[accepted_culture|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[non_accepted_culture|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[tolerated_culture|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[foreign_culture|e]

name: Assimilate
description:
This is the process where [pops|e] of one [culture|e] change over time to the [primary_culture|e] of the [country|e] that [owns|e] them.

It is sped up if the [primary_culture] has a high [culture_war_power|e] versus the [pop|e] culture.

Some specific [cultures|e] are directly tied to their [faith|e], so they will not be able to be assimilated unless they are [converted|e] first.

A culture must either be present in a country or have a neutral or higher opinion of the player to be selectable.

name: Conversion
description: This is the process by which [pops|e] change from one [religion|e] to another over time. The [cabinet|e] is the most reliable medium for a [country|e] to influence $game_concept_conversion$, but [laws|e], [privileges|e], [advances|e], and [societal_values|e] also play a substantial role.

name: Location Size
description: The physical size of a [location|e]. Not every location is the same size.

name: Location
description:
The smallest unit of land, and part of a [province|e]. Its base characteristics are defined by [topography|e], [vegetation|e], and [climate|e]. It may also contain a [river|e].

Each Location has a [raw_material|e] which can be gathered by [pops|e] who live there. [buildings|e] can be constructed in Locations and also [employ|e] Pops. Most Locations are [rural|e], but they can also be granted [town_or_city|e] status.

Each Location can be [owned|e] and [controlled|e] by [countries|e], and [armies|e] can move between different Locations to conquer them when there is a [war|e].

name: Capital
description: This is the [location|e] that is at the political center of a [country|e], where the [government|e] resides. Getting it [occupied|e] in a [war|e] can be devastating.

name: Price
description: A price is something that a [country|e] pays for an activity. A price can be [gold|e], [manpower|e], impact on [stability|e], or other things.

name: Subunit
description: Subunits are the distinct troops in the [unit|e] which fight either as [regiments|e] or as [ships|e]. They are always of a specific [unit_type|e] and as such belong to a [unit_category|e].

name: Unit Formation Preference
description: This determines the Formation logic that is applied when using the #W $BALANCE_ARMY$#! action, or when the Formation of your Units is automated.

name: Unit
description: A unit can either be an [army|e] or a [navy|e]. It is made up of [sub_units|e].

name: Army
description: An army is a group of [regiments|e] led by a [character|e], which can fight [battles|e] and [siege|e] down enemy [fortifications|e].

name: Regular Army
description: Refers to the standing [army|e] that a [country|e] has, excluding [levies|e].

name: Regular Ship
description: Regular Ships are recruited manually by a [country|e] using [sailors|e] and [gold|e]. These form the standing [navies|e], and are rather limited in numbers until you get the [advances|e] from later [ages|e].

name: Navy
description: Navies are what allows a [country|e] to project power beyond its own land. Navies are groups of [ships|e] led by a [character|e], which can fight [battles|e], [blockade|e] [hostile|e] coasts, disrupt enemy [maritime_presence|e], and transport [armies|e] where they are needed. They also help with logistics as they can [distribute_food|e] and [gather_food|e].

name: Regiment
description: A regiment is the building block of an [army|e]. Each has a [maximum_strength|e] of [manpower|e] and is of a specified [unit_type|e]. They can either be an [army_levy|e], a [mercenary|e], or a [regular_regiment|e].

name: Ship
description: This is the main building block of a [navy|e]. A ship is a large boat able to carry [food|e], [regiments|e], and its own crew. Each ship is of a specific [ship_type|e].

name: Military Objective
description: [armies|e] and [navies|e] can be assigned objectives that they will attempt to fulfill on their own.

name: Topography
description: Topography represents the roughness and elevation of the land within a [location|e]. Flatter Topography is generally better for growing [towns_and_cities|e], while rougher Topography is easier to defend.

name: Vegetation
description: Vegetation represents the foliage cover of a [location|e].

name: Climate
description:
$game_concept_climate_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('climate')]

name: Construction
description:
The process of building something in a [location|e], such as a [building|e], a [regiment|e], or a [ShowLocationRankName('city')].

Constructions require [goods|e] from the [market|e] of the [location|e] in which they are taking place. If the needed [goods] aren't available, [construction] will stall.

name: Unit Type
description: Each [unit_category|e] contains lots of variations when it comes to type. Different types come from [advances|e], [culture|E], or from other sources. The type is what makes a unit unique, and what gives it its abilities and attributes. Some examples for [ships|e] include [ShowUnitDefinitionName('n_cog')], [ShowUnitDefinitionName('n_twodecker')], and [ShowUnitDefinitionName('n_xebec')], while [regiments|e] include [ShowUnitDefinitionName('a_arquebusiers')] and [ShowUnitDefinitionName('a_cavaliers')] amongst many more.

name: Unit Template
description: A unit template is a collection of [unit_types|e] that can be used to recruit different [units|e] directly. It can be used to create both [regiments|e] and [ships|e].

name: Unit Category
description:
$game_concept_unit_category_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('unit_category')]

name: Provincial Food
description:
This is the amount of [food|e] that a [province|e] has stored. If the [monthly_food|e] is negative, it will eventually be depleted. If there is a deficit, the province will [buy_food|e] from the local [market|e] and if there is a surplus, it will [sell_food|e].

Any [food] that is not consumed by the [pops|e] in a [location|e] is contributed to the Provincial Food storage.

All territories in the Province can draw from this storage to feed their inhabitants. [armies|e] in the province can also consume stored food if they would otherwise suffer [attrition|e].

name: Food Stockpile
description:
Monthly [food|e] surplus from @location! [locations|e] is stored in the @province! [province|e] Stockpile. Monthly [food] surplus from the [provinces] is stored in the @market! [market|e] Stockpile.

A large enough [food_stockpile] may help prevent [starvation|e] during a harsh [winter|e], when the [food_productivity|e] is low.

A higher $game_concept_food_stockpile$ in a @province! [province|e] also allows it to [buy_food|e] and [sell_food|e] in larger quantities each month.

name: Food Decay
description: [food|e] does not last forever, and some are spoiled every month.

name: Food
Local Food
description:
This is the amount of [food|e] that a [location|e] contributes to the [provincial_food|e]. If it is negative, the $game_concept_location$ will simply take $game_concept_food$ from other $game_concept_locations$ in its [province|e].

Every $game_concept_location$ produces some $game_concept_food$ depending on its [subsistence_agriculture|e] and its [food_productivity|e], but the bulk of the $game_concept_food$ production happens in $game_concept_locations$ with [food_raw_materials|e].

Every $game_concept_location$ will also have some [pop_food_consumption|e] depending on the [population|e] living therein.

[towns_and_cities|e] will often have negative $game_concept_local_food$ balances, but that is not a problem as long as the $game_concept_provincial_food$ is positive.

name: Food Productivity
description:
The $game_concept_food_productivity$ of a [location|e] impacts how efficient it is at producing [food|e].

It depends mostly on the geography of the $game_concept_location$, but some [laws|e], [societal_values|e], and [advances|e] can also affect it. [towns_and_cities|e] are less efficient at producing $game_concept_food$ than [rural_locations|e].

name: Food Capacity
description: This is how much [food|e] a [unit|e] can carry with them as they move.

name: Food Source
description: An [army|e] will gather food from a [province|e] where it has [food_access|e], a friendly [supply_depot|e] or a [navy|e] that is [distributing_food|e].

name: Logistics Distance
description: This is how far away an [army|e] can trace its supply lines to a [food_source|e]. Armies will gather food from a [province|e] where it has [food_access|e], a friendly [supply_depot|e], or a [navy|e] that is [distributing_food|e]. A [hostile|e] army or [zone_of_control|e] will block this.

name: Construction Material
description: $game_concept_construction_materials$ are [raw_materials|e] which play a significant role in the [construction|e] of [buildings|e]. They are produced in a [rgo|e], and are usually essential for the development of [towns_and_cities|e].

name: Food Raw Material
description:
On top of being traded and used like the other [goods|e], some [raw_materials|e] also produce [food|e]. They are produced in a [rgo|e], and constitute a much more efficient source of $game_concept_food$ than [subsistence_agriculture|e].

$game_concept_food$ is also moved between [markets|e] when $game_concept_food_raw_materials$ are traded.

name: Experience
description:
Experience reduces the [damage_taken|e] in a [battle|e], and is primarily gained through participating in a [battle], a [siege|e], or a [blockade|e]. Over time, the experience of a [regiment|e] or [ship|e] will slowly decay.
[regiments] can also gain experience by the [ShowUnitAbilityName('drill_army')] [unit_ability|e].
With some [recruitment_methods|e], a new unit can start with a higher level of experience.

name: Morale
description:
Morale is how long an [army|e] or [navy|e] will fight before giving up.

In [battle|e], every [regiment|e] or [ship|e] inflicts [morale_damage_done|e] upon its opponent, the effect of which is modified by the opponent's [morale_damage_taken|e]. Once Morale hits zero, the Army or Navy will [retreat|e] and lose the [battle].

name: Locked
description: An [army|e] or [navy|e] that has been locked can not be given orders. You have to wait until you get access to that unit again.

name: Language
description:
Each [culture|E] has a [language] they may share with other [cultures]. The [language] has a [language_power|e], and any number of [dialects|e] which determine [character|e] names.

A [country|e] can have a [court_language|e], a [liturgical_language|e], and shares its [common_language|e] with its [primary_culture|e].

Some languages belong to a [language_family|e], whereas some others are [isolated_language_short|e].

name: Language Family
description:
A Language Family is a set of [languages|e] that have descended from a common ancestor and therefore may share a lot of similarities.

Some [languages] do not belong to a [language_family_short] and are therefore [isolated_language|e].

name: Isolated Language
description: A [language|e] is [isolated_language_short] when it does not share a [language_family|e] with other [languages].

name: Dialect
description: A [dialect] is a variation on a [language|e]. It mostly affects the names of things like [characters|e] and [locations|e].

name: Language Power
description:
Language Power represents the reach, influence, and prestige of a [language|e]. It is expressed as a percentage relative to the most powerful Language in the world.

It is calculated by the total [political_power|e] of [pops|e] with the [primary_culture|e] in [countries|e] where it is the [court_language|e], and the number of Clergy following the [primary_religion|e] in Countries where it is the [liturgical_language|e].

Having a [liturgical_language] with high Language Power increases the speed of [research|e], while a [court_language] with high Language Power increases the [estate_satisfaction|e] of the Nobility.

name: Liturgical Language
description: This is the official [language|e] that a [country|e] uses for their official [religion|e]. Some religions, like [ShowReligionName('catholic')], have a fixed $game_concept_liturgical_language$ that can not be changed, but other religions allow countries to change it. The [language_power|e] of the $game_concept_liturgical_language$ of a Country impacts the speed of how quickly they [research|e] new [advances|e].

name: Liturgical Dialect
description: The main [dialect|e] of a [country|e]'s [liturgical_language|e].

name: Common Language
description: This is the [language|e] of the [primary_culture|e] in a [country|e]. If this is the [court_language|e] then the [ShowEstateTypeName('peasants_estate')] will be happy.

name: Court Language
description:
The [language_with_icon|e] of government in a [country_with_icon|e].

Certain Languages may affect the [estate_satisfaction|e] of different [estates|e]:
$BULLET$The [ShowEstateTypeName('nobles_estate')] prefer high [language_power_with_icon|e].
$BULLET$The [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')] prefer the [liturgical_language_with_icon|e].
$BULLET$The [ShowEstateTypeName('peasants_estate')] prefer the [common_language_with_icon|e].
$BULLET$Using the [market_language_with_icon|e] of our [capital] will increase the [selling_efficiency|e].

The Court Language receives an increase in its [language_power] relative to the total [political_power|e] of [pops|e] belonging to the [primary_culture|e] of the Country.

We can change our Court Language to:
$BULLET$[common_language],
$BULLET$[liturgical_language],
$BULLET$[dominant_dialect|e],
$BULLET$The [market_language|e] of our [capital],
$BULLET$The language of an [accepted_culture|e],
$BULLET$Our ruler's language,
$BULLET$Our dynasty head's language,
$BULLET$The [court_language] of an [international_organization_leader|e],
$BULLET$The [court_language] of our [overlord|e].

name: Court Dialect
description: The main [dialect|e] of a [country|e]'s [court_language|e].

name: Foreign Language
description: A [language|e] that is neither the [common_language|e] nor the [liturgical_language|e] of a [country|e] will be considered a $game_concept_foreign_language$.

name: Country Strength
description: This is an estimate of the power of a [country|e]. It takes into account its [military_strength|e], [income|e], and [population|e].

name: Military Strength
description: The Military Strength of a [country|e] is calculated from its maximum [manpower|e], [army|e] size, and [levy|e] power.

name: Naval Strength
description: The Naval Strength of a [country|e] is calculated from its maximum [sailors|e], [navy|e] size, and [navy_levy|e] power.

name: Civil Construction
description: Civil Constructions are anything that is currently being built in a [location|e] that is not an [army|e] or [navy|e] unit, for example [buildings|e], moving your [capital|e], creating a [market|e] or building [roads|e].

name: Market Language
description:
This is the [language|e] spoken by the majority of the [ShowPopTypeName('burghers')] in the [market_center|e].

[ShowPopTypeNameWithNoTooltip('burghers')] who already speak their market's $game_concept_market_language$ are reluctant to give it up. Their [assimilate|e] rate toward cultures that don't share that language is reduced in proportion to the location's [market_access|e] — strong commercial ties slow assimilation, while weak ties barely affect it.

name: Cultural Tradition
description:
This is the defense power of a [culture|e] in the context of [culture_war|e], representing how strongly this culture's traditions resonate with its people.

Tradition has a monthly change dependent on relevant [buildings|e], [societal_values|e], [advances|e], and many other factors.

name: Cultural Influence
description:
This is the attack power of a [culture|e] in the context of [culture_war|e], representing how impressive it appears to other cultures, and the reach it has beyond its own borders.

It has a monthly increase upon the completion of a [work_of_art|e] and has some monthly increase from many sources such as [prestige|e], and certain [buildings|e], [advances|e], [laws|e], and many others. But beware, it also has a natural monthly decay.

name: Culture War Power
description:
This is the strength of an attacking [culture|e]'s [cultural_influence|e] against a target [culture]'s [cultural_tradition|e].

Having a high Culture War Power impacts processes like [assimilation|e], [integration|e], [spy_networks|e], [diplomacy|e], and even [siege|e].

name: Character
description:
A Character is an individual [person|e] possessing [abilities|e], [traits|e], [culture|e], and [religion|e]. They may even belong to a [dynasty|e] if they are of noble bearing.

Once they become an [adult|e], they may be a [ruler|e] or [regent|e], or may be assigned a role in [cabinet|e], or as a [general|e] or [admiral|e].

[adults] may also [marry|e] and produce [children|e].

name: Infiltrate Administration
description: This allows us to remove [fog_of_war|e] over another [country|e] for a period of time.

name: Conquer
description:
This is when a [location|e] changes [owner|e] from one [country|e] to another. This is usually through a [peace_treaty|e] after a [war|e], but there are other ways, such as selling [locations] via [diplomacy].

A Conquered [location] needs to be [integrated|e] in order to be governed effectively.

name: Owner
description: The [country|e] that is recognized to have de jure possession over a [location|e]. Even if the [controller|e] currently may be another country.

name: Controller
description:
The [country|e] currently able to exercise de facto power over a [location|e].

Typically, this is the [owner|e], but during a [war|e] this could become an [enemy|e] if the [location] becomes [occupied|e].

name: Courtier
description: Any [character|e] in a [country|e] who does not hold a specific [role|e] is considered a $game_concept_courtier$. $game_concept_courtiers$ can be employed as [cabinet_members|e], [generals|e], [admirals|e], or [explorers|e].

name: Consort
description: A Consort is a [character|e] who is [married|e] to a [ruler|e]. In some forms of governments, they may get powers, but in most cases, they are there to help provide [heirs|e].

name: Heir
description:
The [character|e] who is next in line to be the [ruler|e] when the current [ruler] dies or abdicates. The order of succession is determined by the [heir_selection|e] of the [government|e].

If succession occurs, but there is no valid heir, or the heir is a [child|e], a [regency|e] is triggered.

name: Eligibility Rules
description: The $game_concept_eligibility_rules$ of a [heir_selection|e] determine which [characters|e] are eligible to become [heir|e] of a [country|e].

name: Dynasty
description: It is a group of characters who share a common ancestor and are thus blood-related. The most important [character|e] in a dynasty is the [dynasty_head|e].

name: Dynastic Power
description: $game_concept_dynastic_power$ is the value of political power a [dynasty|e] holds in an [international_organization|e]. It plays a major role within the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetName], and is calculated by multiplying the [great_power_score|e] and ownership over [pops|e] within the [international_organization] [countries|e] have.

name: Dynasty Founder
description: The Founder of the [dynasty|E].

name: Head of the Dynasty
description: This is the most prestigious and important [character|e] in the [dynasty|e]. The [dialect|e] of a dynasty is defined by that of its $game_concept_dynasty_head$, and some [events|e] and other content may require a $game_concept_dynasty_head$.

name: Dynastic Seat
description: Every Dynasty has its ancestral home in a specific [location|e]. Those [locations] that harbor a $game_concept_dynasty_seat$ will have more [ShowPopTypeName('nobles')] than usual.

name: Lowborn
description: This is a [character|e] who does not belong to any [dynasty|e] of note.

name: Government
description:
Every [country|e] has a Government of a specific [government_type|e] located in its [capital|e].

Governments consist of the [ruler|e] and the [cabinet|e], and are shaped by [societal_values|e], [government_reforms|e], and [laws|e].

name: Government Type
description:
$game_concept_government_type_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('government_type')]

name: International Organization
description: A group of [countries|e] that have banded together in some kind of agreement, sometimes targeting another [country].

name: Election
description:
Some [heir_selections|e] may require an election to decide which [character|e] should be the next [ruler|e].

Depending on the rules of the [heir_selection], an election may occur at regular intervals, or upon the death of the previous [ruler].

If there is no [ruler], then the [government|e] will temporarily be ruled by a [regency|e] until the election concludes.

name: International Organization Type
description:
$game_concept_international_organization_type_upper_title$

$game_concept_international_organization_type_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabaseWithIcon('international_organization_type')]

name: Member
description: These are the [countries|e] that are part of an [international_organization|e].

name: Elector
description: These are the [members|e] who enjoy the [special_status|e] which allows them to decide who will be the next [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e].

name: Imperial Religion
description: The Imperial Religion determines what [religion|e] a [member|e] has to follow to be able to be elected to become the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of the [holy_roman_empire|e]. It is also possible that the Imperial Religion can either be a [religion_group|e] or can be completely abolished, making religion a non-deciding factor in the voting process.

name: Leader Type
description:
This determines who actually is the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e]. There are three types of leadership for International Organizations:
- #Y $LEADER_TYPE_CHARACTER$#! - The organization is led by a [character|e] and the country it belongs to
- #Y $LEADER_TYPE_COUNTRY$#! - The organization is led by determined [country|e] which is in charge even if its own [ruler|e] gets replaced
- #Y $LEADER_TYPE_NONE$#! - The organization is in a perpetual state of an interregnum and neither character nor country will represent the organization

name: Leader Change Method
description:
This determines how the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e] gets chosen. There are five methods to accomplish this:
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_METHOD_ROTATION$#! - The current leader will be the last in line for leadership once their turn is up
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_METHOD_VOTE$#! - The leader will be elected via a [leadership_election_resolution|e]
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_METHOD_LOTTERY$#! - The leader will be chosen from possible candidates at random
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_METHOD_SCORE$#! - The leader will be chosen dynamically based on an internal point system specific to the International Organization
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_METHOD_NONE$#! - The terms of how a leader for the International Organization is chosen are not defined, as no leader is needed or the International Organization has not codified the leadership yet

name: Leader Change Trigger
description:
This determines under what conditions the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e] gets changed. There are three triggers when the leader could change:
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_TRIGGER_TYPE_RULER_CHANGE$#! - Whenever the ruler changes, a new leader for the International Organization is considered
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_TRIGGER_TYPE_TIMED$#! - A new leader of the International Organization is considered after a set amount of months
- #Y $LEADER_CHANGE_TRIGGER_TYPE_NONE$#! - The leader remains in power indefinitely

name: Leadership Election Resolution
description: This is the special [resolution|e] used to determine how the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e] is elected.

name: Candidate
description: These are the [countries|e] that are currently considered as the next [international_organization_leader_short|e] of an [international_organization|e].

name: Free City
description: $free_city_desc$

name: God
description: A God, Goddess, or Deity, is a supernatural being serving as a focus of worship for any particular religion, and usually assigned powers of control over certain aspects of the universe or human existence.

name: Omen
description: $game_concept_omens$ are phenomena in the [ShowReligionAdjective('hellenism_religion')] [religion|e] associated with [gods|e]. They are summoned with [ShowGenericActionName('select_omen_god')] and [ShowGenericActionName('select_omen')]. Their power is increased by the [ability|e] of the [ruler|e].

name: Offered Omens
description: The number of [omens|e] our country can have summoned at the same time. Set by the $MODIFIER_TYPE_NAME_omens_offered$ modifier from our [religion|e] and [religious_aspects|e].

name: Avatar
description: Avatars are the different aspects, manifestations, or incarnations that a particular [god|e] can take in [ShowReligionName('hindu')].

name: Bureaucracy
description:
A $game_concept_bureaucracy$ is a branch of the [government|e] that grows over time, draws money from the [balance|e], and provides good and bad modifiers with dynamic strength.

Each $game_concept_bureaucracy$ has positive, negative, and constant modifiers. Constant modifiers are constant.

The amount of [gold|e] spent on [bureaucracy_maintenance_short|e] impacts whether the negative or positive modifier is more dominant.

[entrenchment|e] increases steadily over time, increasing the cost, but also increasing the power of both positive and negative modifiers. A $game_concept_bureaucracy$ with higher $game_concept_entrenchment$ is also more costly to remove.

[estates|e] may like or dislike active $game_concept_bureaucracies$, which will impact their [estate_satisfaction|e] relative to the $game_concept_entrenchment$. They may also ask to increase or reduce the $game_concept_entrenchment$ via [parliament_agendas|e].

name: Bureaucracy Type
description: A $game_concept_bureaucracy_type$ is the blueprint of a [bureaucracy|e], and defines its characteristics.

name: Disease
description: A disease can wreak havoc on our [people|e]. Different diseases have different specified chances of an [outbreak|e], method, and likelihood of transmission and mortality rate. Their terrible effects can be reduced with [disease_resistance|e].

name: Disease Outbreak
description: When a [disease|e] breaks out in a particular [location|e], it can then spread from there by various means...and it may or may not claim victims along the way.

name: Holy Site
description: A place that is of special interest to a particular [religion|e]. A Holy Site may provide various bonuses to the [location|e] or [owner|e], which are scaled by its [holy_site_importance_short|e].

name: Holy Site Type
description:
$game_concept_holy_site_type_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('holy_site_type')]

name: $game_concept_holy_site$ $game_concept_holy_site_importance_short$
description: The $game_concept_holy_site_importance_short$ of a [holy_site|e] scales any bonuses that apply in its [location|e] or [owner|e].

name: Succession Law
description:
Every [government|e] has a Succession Law which defines which [character|e] shall be the next [ruler|e] once the current one dies or abdicates.

Many Succession Laws define an [heir|e] before the succession occurs based on the [heir_selection_score|e] of that character, while others trigger an [election|e].

Each different Succession Law has its own rules, such as whether an heir may be of the same [dynasty|e], or if they must belong to specific [estates|e].

A [country|e] may select another Succession Law; the options available can be influenced by factors such as the current [government_type|e] and any active [government_reforms|e].

name: Heir Score
description: The $game_concept_heir_selection_score$ determines how much the [character|e] is favored to be elected by the [heir_selection|e] of a [country|e]. Usually, the character with the highest score becomes the new [ruler|e] upon a succession.

name: Population Capacity
description: This is the amount of [population|e] a [location|e] can support. If the [population] is higher than this, it will not be able to grow more, and if it is too high it may even decrease.

name: Total Population
description: This is the total amount of [pops|e] that live in a [country|e].

name: Population
description: The population of a [location|e] is the total amount [pops|e] living there.

name: People
description: Individual human beings. Semi-renewable resource, grouped in [pops|e] or may appear as [characters|e].

name: Pop
description: A Pop is a group of [people|e] of the same [pop_type|e], [religion|e], and [culture|e]. They have needs for various [goods|e], and their [pop_satisfaction|e] impacts the [location|e] they live in.

name: Trade
description:
A trade is the movement of a [good|e] from one [market|e] to another. The goods are bought in one market and then sold in the other, hopefully giving a [trade_profit|e] to the owner of the trade. The amount of [merchant_capacity|e] required for the trade depends both on the distance between the markets and the amount of [goods] that the trade is handling.

[trade_income|e] is split between the Crown and the [estates_with_icon|e] according to their [estate_power_with_icon|e]. Only the percentage of [crown_power_with_icon|e] goes to the [treasury|e].

name: Import
description: An Import is a [trade|e] moving [goods|e] into a [market|e], and thus increasing its [supply|e] in that [market].

name: Export
description:
An Export is a [trade|e] moving [goods|e] out from a [market|e], and thus increasing its [demand|e] in that [market].

If there are multiple trades trying to export the same goods, then the goods are given in order of [merchant_power|e].

name: $burghers$ Trading
description: The [ShowPopTypeName('burghers')] will attempt to address needs for [goods|e] in the [market|e] that their [town_or_city|e] is located in, by doing their own [trades|e].

name: Common Goods
description: Some [goods|e] like [ShowGoodsName('stone')] or [ShowGoodsName('clay')] can be produced everywhere without the need for an [rgo|e], and this is considered a common good. As normal $game_concept_goods$, they are then provided to the [market|e].

name: Trade Orders
description: Trade Orders allow you to allocate [merchant_capacity|e] to automatically [import|e] or [export|e] a specific [good|e] without specifying a destination. The AI will pick the best route each day.

name: Trade Income
description:
This is the money gained from [trades_with_icon|e] when selling [goods_with_icon|e] to [markets_with_icon|e].

Trade income is split between the Crown and the [estates_with_icon|e] according to their [estate_power_with_icon|e]. Only the percentage of [crown_power_with_icon|e] goes to the [treasury|e].

name: Trade Expense
description: This is the money spent on [trades|e], buying [goods|e] from [markets|e], and the cost of the [merchant_maintenance|e].

name: Goods
description:
Goods can be either [raw_materials|e] that are farmed, gathered, mined, logged, or hunted for, or [produced_goods|e] which are primarily created in towns or cities.

The [food_raw_materials|e] are also a source of [food|e].

name: Raw Goods
description: Every [location|e] [produces|e] one type of $game_concept_raw_material$. The amount that it [produces] depends on how much that [location|e] has been developed. What differs raw materials from [produced_goods|e] is that they do not require [buildings|e] to be produced, and rely solely on [rgo_pops|e]. There are some $game_concept_raw_materials$, though, that can also be produced by [buildings].

name: Occupation
description:
Occupation is when the [controller|e] of a [location|e] is different from its [owner|e]. This happens when a [location] falls within the [zone_of_control] of a [fortification|e] that is [controlled] by an [enemy|e], or when an [army|e] successfully [sieges|e] the location.

In many cases, a [location|e] needs to be occupied before it can be added to a [peace_treaty|e].

name: Produced Goods
description: This is a type of [goods|e] that is produced by [pops|e] working in a [building|e]. In many cases, those buildings require [raw_materials|e] or other Produced Goods to function.

name: Attacker
description: The Attacker in a [battle|e] may have several disadvantages, as they will get any [topography|e], [vegetation|e], or [crossing|e] penalties. The other side is referred to as the [defender|e].

name: Defender
description: The Defender in a [battle|e] will avoid the penalties that the [attacker|e] may get. Usually, the defender is the [army|e] or [navy|e] that is first present in a [location|e], unless they are busy in a [siege|e].

name: Crossing
description:
An [army|e] crossing a river between two [locations|e], crossing a [strait|e], or landing from a [seazone|e] will get a penalty in [battle|e] if they are the [attacker|e].

Crossing a [river] imposes a penalty on the [attacker] of [GetDefine('NCombat','RIVER_CROSSING_DICE')|R] on the dice roll. Crossing a [strait] imposes a penalty of [GetDefine('NCombat','STRAIT_CROSSING_DICE')|R].

name: Combat
description:
If two or more [armies|e] meet in a [location|e], or two or more [navies|e] in a [seazone|e], and they are [hostile|e] towards each other, a battle will start between them.
The battle usually starts with a [bombard_phase|e] and then continues in the [combat_phase|e]. Each [regiment|e] or [ship|e] will attempt to [engage|e] the enemy, and fight until one side [retreats|e].

name: Siege
description:
A siege occurs when an [army|e] arrives in a [location|e] when the [controller|e] and the $game_concept_army$ are [enemies|e].

A siege against a $game_concept_location$ without a [fortification|e] will take about a month, but if there is a $game_concept_fortification$ present it will take far longer, depending on the level of the $game_concept_fortification$.

If the $game_concept_army$ wins against a $game_concept_location$ [owned|e] by the $game_concept_enemy$, it will then become [occupied|e] and it will increase the [war_score|e] for the $game_concept_army$'s $game_concept_owner$.

For a [siege|e] to progress there needs to be at least as many men besieging it as the number of men in the [garrison|e]. For a [location|e] without [fortifications|e], there needs to be at least #V 100#! men.

name: Assault
description: An assault is when the attacker in a [siege|e] tries to storm the [fortification|e] in order to take it as quickly as possible. An assault can be rather costly, as the attacker will take heavy casualties.

name: Garrison
description:
These are the soldiers that are working with defending the [fortifications|e] of a [location|e]. When they are all killed, or their [morale|e] is gone, the [siege|e] will be lost for the defender.

For a [siege|e] to progress there needs to be at least as many men besieging it as the number of men in the [garrison|e]. For a [location|e] without [fortifications|e], there needs to be at least #V 100#! men.

name: Reinforce
description: When a [regiment|e] is below its [maximum_strength|e], it will attempt to reinforce, by drawing [manpower|e] and [gold|e] from its [country|e]. Only a [regular_regiment|e] can reinforce, and unless in a [friendly|e] [location|e] it will not be possible.

name: Repair
description: When a [ship|e] is damaged, it can be repaired in one of our own [ports|e] or where we have [fleet_basing_rights|e], by drawing [sailors|e] and [gold|e] from its [country|e].

name: Prosperity
description:
Prosperity represents how prosperous and resourceful a [location|e] is. Positive Prosperity increases the [development|e] of the [location] over time and makes it more likely to attract [migration|e].

Prosperity rises naturally over time, but will decrease as a result of low [pop_satisfaction|e], [diseases|e], [sieges|e], [occupation|e], [blockades|e], or if the [location] is [looted|e] by an enemy [army|e]. Negative Prosperity can have devastating consequences for the [population|e] of the [location].

name: Development
description: Development represents how cultivated the land is, and how much it is used by the [pops|e] living there. The higher the development, the more people can live there, and the more it can be exploited.

name: Power Projection
description: [countries|e] with higher $game_concept_power_projection$ can exploit nations with less. If ours is higher than another nation's, then we will be able to build a [ShowBuildingTypeName('trade_office')], [ShowBuildingTypeName('slave_center')], [ShowBuildingTypeName('missionary_building')], or other specific buildings in their [locations|e]. The higher our $game_concept_power_projection$ is, the quicker our [colonial_charters|e] can take control over locations. Having a higher $game_concept_power_projection$ than another country also reduces the [stability|e] cost of declaring [war|e] upon them, as well as the [war_exhaustion|e].

name: Control
description:
The control that the [owner|e] of a [location|e] has determines the [tax_base|e], [army_levies|e], and [navy_levies|e] available in the [location]. It also affects the speed of [promotion|e], [assimilation|e], and [conversion|e], as well as the amount of monthly [manpower|e] and [sailors|e] it gives. The Control of a Location will slowly change towards its [max_control|e], meaning Control will slowly decrease if it is above the Max, or slowly increase if it is below it.

There are some [buildings|e] that increase Max control, but primarily it depends on the [proximity|e] to the [capital|e] of the [country|e]. Tracing a route through [roads|e] or [maritime_presence|e] along our coasts increases the [proximity|e], increasing the [max_control] of the [location].

name: Maximum Control
description:
The [control] of a [location] will slowly trend towards its Maximum Control. The main source of Maximum Control is [proximity|e], but the [integration_status|e] and [pop_satisfaction|e] also play a role.

The Maximum Control of a Location can be temporarily increased by stationing an Army in the [province|e], as well as with the [ShowCabinetActionName('increase_control_province')] [cabinet_action|e].

name: Proximity
description:
The Proximity of a [location_with_icon|e] measures how close it is to the [capital_with_icon|e] of its [owner|e], and it determines how much [control_with_icon|e] [locations] can have.

[proximity] starts at #high 100%#! in the [capital] of every [country|e], and jumps to nearby [locations], giving them [proximity]. Some [proximity] is lost with every subsequent jump, depending on the terrain and the infrastructure present in the [location]. The [proximity] that is lost in jumping from one [location] to the next is called Proximity Cost.

The Proximity cost between [locations] varies greatly with [topography_with_icon|e] and [vegetation_with_icon|e]. On land, it can be reduced by building [roads_with_icon|e], increasing [development_with_icon|e], and the [ShowSocietyDirectionName('land')] [societal_value_with_icon|e]. On sea, it can be reduced by [harbor_capacity_with_icon|e], [maritime_presence_with_icon|e] and the [ShowSocietyDirectionName('naval')] [societal_value].

name: Road
description: A road is a built connection between two [locations|e]. These make it easier for a [country|e] to exert [control|e] over its territory, make [trade|e] easier, and allow [armies|e] to march faster.

name: Employment System
description: This describes how [locations|e] fill their [buildings|e] with workers.

name: Military Stance
description: This describes how [subjects|e] decide what to do for their [overlords|e] in times of [war|e].

name: Foreign Building
description: This is a [building|e] that belongs to a [country|e] different from the [owner|e] of the [location|e].

name: Building Type
description: A Building Type is the blueprint of a [building|e], and belongs to a [building_category|e]. Most of a [building]'s features are dependent on what Building Type it is.

name: Building
description:
Buildings are unique examples of [building_types|e] in a [location|e].

Buildings have a wide variety of different functions, from increasing the [supply|e] of manufactured [goods|e] to unlocking unique [unit_types|e]. Their efficiency is based on how many [pops|e] are currently [employed|e] there.

Most buildings have an upfront construction cost in [gold|e], and thereafter place additional [demand|e] upon certain [goods] in the [location]'s [market|e]. If a building runs at a loss, its [owner|e] may [subsidize|e] it.

[estates|e] may also construct buildings.

Buildings can also be destroyed.

A building has one or more [production_methods|e] that can be changed, which impacts its output.

name: Building Maintenance
description: [buildings] that do not produce [goods|e] incur an upkeep cost for their [owner]. The cost depends on the [market_price|e] of the [goods] used by the building, and is affected by the [crown_power|e] of the owner.

name: Supported Building Levels
description:
Every [location|e] has a soft limit on the number of [building|e] levels it can contain. Surpassing that limit will incur progressively higher construction prices.

The number of $game_concept_supported_building_levels$ depends primarily on the [location_rank|e] and the [development|e] of the [location].

[buildings] without workers do not count towards the building level limit.

name: Employ
description: [pops|e] can be employed either in a [building|e] or in an [rgo|e]. A building can only support one [pop_type|e], and the maximum amount depends on the type of building and how many levels it has.

name: Available Population
description: [pops|e] can be [employed|e] either in a [building|e] or in an [rgo|e]. Those that are not doing that are considered $game_concept_available$.

name: Foreign
description: This is a [location|e] that is not owned by the [country|e] you are playing.

name: Dominant Upper Class Culture
description:
The dominant [upper_class|e] culture is the largest [culture|e] in a [country|e] of all the upper class [pops|e], scaled by the [control|e] of the [locations|e] they are present in, as well as the innate [political_power|e] of the [estate|e] they belong to.

This does not necessarily mean that it is the majority.

name: Upper Class
description:
This is a group of [pop_types|e] that belong to one of the [estates|e] that usually have the most power in a [country|e], and are one of the following [pop_types]:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('nobles')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('clergy')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('burghers')]

name: Lower Class
description:
This is a group of [pop_types|e] that belong to the lower strata of society, including the following [pop_types]:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('laborers')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('soldiers')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('peasants')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('tribesmen')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('slaves')]

name: Social Class
description:
$game_concept_pop_type_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('pop_type')]

name: Pop Food Consumption
description: This is how much [food|e] a [pop|e] will consume each month.

name: Estate
description:
Special interest groups within a [country_with_icon|e], Estates have [estate_power_with_icon|e] representing their political strength within government, [estate_satisfaction_with_icon|e] representing how well their needs are fulfilled, an [estate_culture_with_icon|e] and [estate_religion_with_icon|e] inherited from their dominant [pops|e], and [estate_opinions|e] of other Countries.

Estates may also have [estate_privileges_with_icon|e], which are special rights that increase their power and can be granted or revoked by the government. In turn, [estates] provide [taxes_with_icon|e], [army_levies_with_icon|e], and [navy_levies_with_icon|e] to their [country].

Estates collect the [tax_base_with_icon|e] from the [locations_with_icon|e], as well as part of the profit of [trade|e], and they use that wealth to build [buildings_with_icon|e] and pay for [pop_needs_with_icon|e]. If their [estate_satisfaction] is low, they will only build estate buildings to support their own [estate_power].

Each [character_with_icon|e] belongs to one of the Estates and increase its power when appointed to the [cabinet_with_icon|e], or when commanding [armies|e] and [navies|e]. Some [heir_selections|e] limit their [heirs|e] to specific estates.

name: Wealth Impact
description:
Wealth Impact is the ratio between an [estate|e]'s monthly [gold|e] income and its monthly expenses.

A value above 100% means the estate earns more than it spends, letting it accumulate wealth and invest in [buildings|e] and [roads|e]. A low Wealth Impact makes an estate cautious, restricting it to building only for its own [estate_power|e] and limiting how much it is willing to fund.

name: Estates Enrichment
description: This is how much an [estate|e] can withhold from their taxable income each month.

name: Estate Opinion
description: Estates in a [country|e] will have opinions about other Countries, i.e. which to be [hostile|e] against and which to befriend, all to further their own needs.

name: Estate Culture
description:
Each [estate|e] has a dominant Estate Culture, weighted by the [pops|e] holding political weight in a [country|e]. The dominant [language|e] among those pops is picked first, and then the dominant [culture|e] among pops who speak that language.

An estate whose culture is the [primary_culture|e] or an [accepted_culture|e] enjoys higher [estate_satisfaction|e] and [estate_power|e]. A [tolerated_culture|e] is neutral, while any other culture lowers both.

name: Estate Religion
description:
Each [estate|e] has a dominant Estate Religion, picked from whichever [religion|e] holds the most political weight among the estate's [pops|e].

The estate's [estate_satisfaction|e] and [estate_power|e] are modified based on the [country|e]'s tolerance of the estate's religion — [primary_religion_tolerance|e] when it matches the [state_religion|e], [heretic_tolerance|e] when it is a [heretic|e] faith of the same group, and [heathenry_tolerance|e] when it belongs to a different religion group.

name: Estate Building
description:
Estate Buildings are [buildings|e] that are only built and maintained by [estates|e], seeking to increase their [political_power|e]. Their effects usually go against the interests of the [ShowEstateTypeName('crown_estate')]. [estates] will prefer to build them in [locations|e] with low [control|e], and they can be destroyed by the Crown if [control] is high enough, or through a [parliament_agenda|e].

[estates] can also build regular [buildings] and [rgo|e] to increase their income, and to that end they will prefer low [control] [locations] where they already enjoy a high [wealth_share|e].

[estates] pay #W [GetDefine('NEconomy','ESTATE_MAX_PRICE_MULTIPLIER')]#! times the regular construction [price|e].

name: Monthly Food
description: Any [food|e] that is not consumed by the Pops in a territory is contributed to the [provincial_food|e] storage.

name: Loan
description: A loan is the amount of [gold|e] that has been lent from the [lender|e] and will need to be repaid with a monthly [interest|e]. A loan can be helpful when a [country|e] needs [gold|e] immediately. Taking a loan will increase the [debt|e] of the [country].

name: Government Bond
description: A government bond is a form of long-term [debt|e] issued by a [country|e]. Unlike an [estate|e] [loan|e], a bond has no expiry date and is never repaid automatically. The [country|e] receives gold upfront and pays a monthly [bond_interest|e] indefinitely until choosing to redeem the bond by paying back the face value.

name: Bond Interest
description: The monthly [interest|e] rate paid on outstanding [government_bonds|e]. Unlike [estate|e] loan interest, this cost is a drain on the treasury with no recipient — it represents the ongoing cost of sovereign debt.

name: Central Bank
description: A central bank is a [building|e] in the [capital|e] that lets a [country|e] issue [government_bonds|e]. It provides bond capacity, reduces [bond_interest|e], and increases the size of each bond issued.

name: Loan Capacity
description: This is how much money that a [country|e] can [lend|e] from its internal sources. The [estates|e] can invest in this, and will earn all the [interest|e] that a [country|e] pays from these loans. Some [buildings|e], [advances|e] or [government_reforms|e] can impact this as well.

name: Lender
description: This is either a bank lending out [gold|e] to earn an [interest|e] on it, or another [country|e] that is lending it.

name: Borrower
description: This is a [country|e] which owes [gold|e] and has to pay [interest|e] on it, usually to another [country|e] or an [estate|e].

name: Interest
description: This is a fee that each [loan|e] has, which is paid each month to the [lender|e].

name: Debt
description: This is the total amount of [loans|e] a country has, including any remaining [interest|e]. If this debt grows too large, the [country|e] will go [bankrupt|e].

name: Creditworthiness
description: Creditworthiness measures how reliably a [country|e] repays its [debts|e]. It ranges from 0 to 100 with 50 as neutral. Higher values reduce the [interest|e] rate on all [loans|e] and make foreign lenders more willing to offer credit; lower values raise interest rates and make lenders reluctant. Going [bankrupt|e] causes a large drain on creditworthiness that recovers slowly over time.

name: Administrative Ability
description: This [ability|e] represents how good a [character|e] is at handling administrative tasks, how good they are at organizing things, handling the economy, and making a country run.

name: Diplomatic Ability
description: This [ability|e] represents how good a [character|e] is at convincing other people to do certain things. It also represents how liked a character is.

name: Military Ability
description: This [ability|e] represents how good a [character|e] is at understanding the military aspects of life, how they understand tactics, and how they make tough choices.

name: Total Ability
description: The Total Ability of a [character|e] is the sum of all their [adm_short|e], [dip_short|e], and [mil_short|e] [ability|e] scores added together.

name: Inflation
description: Inflation represents the increase in all prices in the game. It is increased by [minting|e] more gold to increase our [income|e], and we can reduce it by a [cabinet_action|e].

name: Prestige
description: The prestige of a [country|e] is how well seen that country is. The [cultural_influence|e] of its [primary_culture|e] is increased by it, and it makes it easier to do [diplomacy|e].

name: Complacency
description:
This represents how complacent the people of a [country|e] has become, when it has no outside threats to care about. Complacency naturally grows with our size and might, and can be kept at bay by having [rivals|e] that pose a [threat|e] to us, increasing our [diplomatic_maintenance|e], and keeping high average [control|e].

High Complacency may inflict heavy penalties upon our [country], but its effects only activate in the context of certain [disasters|e].

[GetComplacencyDisasters]

name: War Enthusiasm
description: This describes the willingness of a [country|e] to continue to pursue this [war|e].

name: War Exhaustion
description:
War Exhaustion represents how much our [country|e] has been ravaged by [war|e]. If it is high enough, we will be forced to sign a [peace_treaty|e]. These are the effects at 1 $game_concept_war_exhaustion$:
[ShowAutoModifierEffect('war_exhaustion_impact')]

name: Stability
description: The stability is a measure of the internal peace of a [country|e]. If it is negative, then it represents turmoil, and if it is positive, tranquility. Over time, stability will tend towards #Y 0#!, unless other factors impact it. Starting [wars|e] is one of the actions that will reduce the stability of a country.

name: In Exile
description: An [army|e] or [navy|e] can be set in Exile, which means that it will be unable to siege or fight any [units|e] until we have moved it back to friendly territory. This happens when they are in territory where they no longer have access to, usually after a [peace_treaty|e] has been signed.

name: Retreat
description: An [army|e] or [navy|e] may be forced to retreat from losing a battle, due to their [morale|e] becoming too low, or it could voluntarily decide to [retreat|e]. While retreating, it will not be able to fight again, or be given new orders, until it has reached its destination.

name: Army Tradition
description: This represents the accumulated experience of [armies|e], [battles|e], and [sieges|e] a [country|e] has.

name: Navy Tradition
description: This represents the accumulated experience of [navies|e], their [battles|e], [blockades|e], and all other naval-related aspects a [country|e] has.

name: Recruit
description: Recruiting is a process to field [manpower|e] as [units|e] on the map. This usually has a [gold|e] cost and a [goods|e] [demand|e] attached to it. After all, a horseman without a horse can barely be called a horseman.

name: Recruitment Method
description: We can decide if we want to spend more time training our troops to increase their [experience|e], or if we want to get the [regiment|e] ready faster, but with lower [maximum_strength|e].

name: Age
description:
$game_concept_age_upper_desc$

[ShowDatabase('age')]

$game_concept_age_lower_desc$

name: Institution
description:
Each [age|e] has three different institutions that will appear in a fitting [location|e] on the map. They will then spread over the map, and as [countries|e] [embrace|e] them, they unlock new [advances|e] for that age.

If we find that an Institution does not spread quickly enough to our [country], we can try to [ShowCabinetActionName('study_institutions')].

name: Embrace
