description: A [country|e] can embrace an [institution|e] when enough of [population|e] of a [country|e] lives in [locations|e] where it has fully spread. This means that the country has fully understood the [institution], and can [research|e] [advances|e] that rely on it.

name: Advance
description:
Advances represent ideas, inventions, technologies, and other areas of human knowledge.

Only one Advance can be [researched|e] at a time, and the speed at which a [country|e] can research them depends on their [research_progress_with_icon|e].

With every [age|e], new Advances become available for [countries] to discover. Some are exclusive to specific [countries], [cultures|e], or [religions|e], but most simply require having [embraced|e] the appropriate [institutions_with_icon|e].

The speed at which we progress towards new [advances_with_icon|e] depends mainly on the power of our [liturgical_language_with_icon|e], the average [literacy_with_icon|e] of our [pops_with_icon|e], the [estate_satisfaction|e] of our [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')], and the number of [institutions_with_icon|e] we have [embraced|e].

name: Research
description:
Researching an [advance|e] takes time, and a [country|e] can only research one advance at a time. We get the benefit of the advance when our [research_progress|e] reaches the cost of the advance.

The speed at which we progress towards new [advances_with_icon|e] depends mainly on the power of our [liturgical_language_with_icon|e], the average [literacy_with_icon|e] of our [pops_with_icon|e], the [estate_satisfaction|e] of our [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')], and the number of [institutions_with_icon|e] we have [embraced|e].

name: Research Progress
description: Our [research_progress|e] depends mainly on the power of our [liturgical_language_with_icon|e], the average [literacy_with_icon|e] of our [pops_with_icon|e], the [estate_satisfaction|e] of our [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')], and the number of [institutions_with_icon|e] we have [embraced|e].

name: Stored Research Progress
description: Stored $game_concept_research_progress$ is accumulated when there is no [advance|e] selected. Stored Research is instantly applied once [advance|e] is selected.

name: Literacy
description: This is how well our [pops|e] can read and write. It is mostly beneficial, as the average literacy in our country impacts our [research_progress|e] positively, but it also increases the impact from the [market_price|e] of their needs on the [pop_satisfaction|e].

name: Artillery Barrage
description: If this is higher than the level of the [fort|e] during a [siege|e], it can give a bonus to the attacker!

name: Artillery Bonus
description: Artillery [regiments|e] have the strength to bombard [fortifications|e] with their guns. The strength depends on their [artillery_barrage|e] and the level of the [fort|e].

name: Combat Phase
description: The Combat Phase is the main [phase|e] of [combat|e] which takes place after the initial [bombard_phase|e]. [regiments|e] or [ships|e] will attempt to [engage|e] their [enemy|e] counterparts.

name: Bombard Phase
description:
The Bombard Phase is the opening [phase|e] of [combat|e] which takes place before the main [combat_phase|e]. It lasts [GetDefine('NCombat','BOMBARD_HOURS')|W] hours and is exclusively utilized by [regiments|e] that can [bombard|e], such as [ShowUnitCategoryName('army_artillery')].

Every hour of the Bombard Phase, valid [regiments] have a chance to [bombard], which will deal their [combat_power|e] as damage to an enemy [regiment] on the same [section|e].

name: Section
description:
Each side in a [combat_with_icon|e] has four Sections: three at the front of the [combat] ([center|e], left [flank|e], and right [flank|e]), and one at the back, the [reserves|e].

During combat, [regiments|e] or [ships|e] in the front Sections will attempt to [engage|e] enemies in the opposite section. If the opposite Section is empty, they can attack any other front Section, where a unit with a good [flanking_ability|e] can do extra damage.

If units get destroyed or withdraw due to too low [morale|e], units from the [reserves] will attempt to move up to replace them by rolling [combat_speed_with_icon|e]. The [combat] ends when there are no more units in the front Sections of one side.

name: Center
description: This is the center [section|e] of a [unit|e]. If there is no opponent in the center, they can easily reach either the left [flank|e] or the right [flank|e].

name: Reserves
description:
These [regiments|e] or [ships|e] are not actively fighting in a [battle|e], but depending on need, they may move up to the [center|e] or either [flank|e].
Each [regiment] or [ship|e] rolls a [d20|e] and if the roll is lower than its [combat_speed|e], it will be able to join the battle. However, only enough units for the possible [frontage|e] of the battle attempts to reinforce each hour.

name: Broken Units
description: These are the [regiments|e] or [ships|e] that have been routed in the current [battle|e]. They will no longer participate in this battle at all.

name: Flank
description: Flanks are the [sections|e] in an [army|e] besides the [center|e]. The left $game_concept_section$ usually fights the right $game_concept_section$ of the opponent and the right $game_concept_section$ usually fights the left $game_concept_section$ of the opponent. However, [flanking_ability|e] also allows damaging adjacent $game_concept_sections$.

name: D100
description: A D100 is a hundred-sided dice roll used to check percentage-based chances.

name: D20
description: A D20 is a twenty-sided dice roll used in [combat|e], when a [regiment|e] or [ship|e] leaves the [reserves|e].

name: D10
description: A D10 is a ten-sided dice roll used in [combat|e], to determine how well a side is doing.

name: Dice
description:
$game_concept_dice_upper_desc$
[d10|e]
[d20|e]
[d100|e]

name: Phase
description: There are two Phases of [combat|e], starting with the initial [GetDefine('NCombat','BOMBARD_HOURS')|W]-hour [bombard_phase|e] (if any [regiments|e] are able to [bombard|e]), followed by the [combat_phase|e].

name: Engagement
description:
When a [combat_with_icon|e] starts, [regiments_with_icon|e] in the front [sections_with_icon|e] roll [initiative_with_icon|e] every hour until they become engaged. When a [regiment] is engaged in [combat], it deals damage. When a unit withdraws, it stops being engaged and will not rejoin the same [combat].

Only a certain amount of [frontage_with_icon|e] can be engaged at once in a [section].

name: Bombard
description: [regiments|e] that can bombard will deal their [combat_power|e] as damage during the opening [bombard_phase|e] of [combat|e].

name: Estate Privilege
description: The [ruler|e] can at times grant certain privileges to certain groups of people. These might be tax breaks, monopolies, or other rights that bestow an advantage to that particular [estate|e]. They generally come at some cost to the crown, be that in the power of the [estate] or some other cost.

name: Supply Depot
description: [armies|e] can create Supply Depots in [hostile|e] [locations|e], where they can deposit and store [food|e]. [friendly|e] armies can then draw on that supply up to #V 2#! [locations] away.

name: Loot
description: When [armies|e] [occupy|e] [locations|e] they will steal [gold|e] from it, and give the [location|e] [ShowModifier('looted')] [modifier|e] for about #V 12#! months.

name: Unit Ability
description: This is the name for orders like [ShowUnitAbilityName('drill_army')] or [ShowUnitAbilityName('march_to_sound_of_guns')], which can be given to [units|e]. Some of these are instant actions, others a state that can be toggled on or off.

name: Character Interaction
description: These are the [actions|e] we can do with a [character|e]. Examples include [ShowCharacterInteractionName('marry_noble')], [ShowCharacterInteractionName('seppuku')], or [ShowCharacterInteractionName('resign_as_grand_master')]

name: Adult
description: A [character|e] who is at least #Y [ShowAdultAge]#! years old is deemed as an adult. They may then serve as [rulers|e] without a [regent|e], become a [general|e] or [admiral|e], or serve in the [cabinet|e], and they can also become [married|e]. A character that is not an adult is considered to be an [infant|e], [child|e], or [adolescent|e].

name: Child
description: A [character|e] who is between the age of #Y [ShowMinChildAge]#! and #Y [ShowMaxChildAge]#! years old is a child. They can not serve their [country|e], but if they belong to the [ruler|e]'s [dynasty|e], you can give them a [child_education|e].

name: Infant
description: A [character|e] who is up to #Y [ShowMaxInfantAge]#! years old is an infant. They can not serve their [country|e] nor receive [child_education|e].

name: Adolescent
description: A [character|e] who is between the age of #Y [ShowMinAdolescentAge]#! and #Y [ShowMaxAdolescentAge]#! years old is an adolescent. They are not yet an [adult|e] but not really a [child|e] anymore.

name: Integration Status
description:
This represents how well a [location|e] is incorporated into the administrative apparatus of its [owner|e]. Every [owned] [location] falls into one of four different status:

$BULLET$[colonized|e]
$BULLET$[conquered|e]
$BULLET$[integrated|e]
$BULLET$[core|e]

Any [conquered] [location] can be [integrated] with a [cabinet_action|e], but reaching [core] status requires a large proportion of [pops|e] of the [primary_culture|e] or any of the [accepted_cultures|e].

name: Integration
description:
An Integrated [location|e] has been properly incorporated into the State, and it is thus much easier to govern than a [conquered|e] [location].

[conquered|e] [locations] need to be Integrated with a [cabinet_action|e] that targets the whole [province|e], and whose speed depends on various factors including the number of [locations], their [culture|e], or their [location_rank|e].

name: Government Reform
description:
Representing everything from ancient traditions to progressive amendments, Government Reforms outline the shape of governance in a [country|e]. Each one is unique, but they often give powerful trade-offs or open up unique play styles.

[countries] are only allowed a handful of Government Reforms, but can increase that allowance with certain [advances|e].

Some reforms are [major_reforms|e]; a [country] may not have more than one of those.

name: Major Reform
description: A Major Reform is a special [government_reform|e] that defines a [country|e]. A [country] may only have one Major Reform at a time.

name: Cabinet Action
description:
A member of the [cabinet|e] can be assigned to a $game_concept_cabinet_action$. These are performed either until they are finished, or until we decide to change it. 
These are the different actions available: 

#T $game_concept_adm_short$ $game_concept_actions$ #!
[ShowCabinetTypeDatabase('adm')] 

#T $game_concept_diplomatic_actions$ #!
[ShowCabinetTypeDatabase('dip')] 

#T $game_concept_mil_short$ $game_concept_actions$ #!
[ShowCabinetTypeDatabase('mil')]

name: Cabinet
description: The $game_concept_cabinet$ is the assembly of higher officials that help govern the [country|e] through [cabinet_actions|e]. The number of [cabinet_seats|e] is increased by [advances|e].

name: Cabinet Member
description: A $game_concept_cabinet_member$ is a [character|e] employed in the [cabinet|e].

name: Cabinet Seats
description: This defines the number of [cabinet_members|e] that a [country|e] can employ simultaneously in its [cabinet|e]. Certain [advances|e] can increase the number of $game_concept_cabinet_seats$ available.

name: Cabinet Efficiency
description: It is the speed and effectiveness with which [characters|e] from the [cabinet|e] will operate when assigned to perform [cabinet_actions|e]. It is influenced by the [crown_power|e] and [societal_values|e], and can also be modified by [advances|e], [government_reforms|e], [policies|e], and [buildings|e].

name: Head of the Cabinet
description:
The Head of the Cabinet is a [character|e] who has been promoted by the court to represent the [cabinet|e].

The [character] receives the following bonuses:
[ShowModifierEffect('head_of_the_cabinet_modifier')]

name: Artist
description:
$game_concept_artist_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('artist')]

name: Religious Figure
description:
$game_concept_religious_figure_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('religious_figures')]

name: Legitimacy
description: Legitimacy is a measure of how accepted the governance is by the population and estates in their [country|e]. It is very much a prerequisite for running a country smoothly - at low levels we will find that nobody wants to work with us and rebellions may break out, attempting to install a [ruler|e] that they find more palatable.

name: Republican Tradition
description: Republican Tradition measures how well Republicanism is entrenched in our country. Republican Tradition represents how strong the traditions are in a [ShowGovernmentTypeName('republic')]. A [ShowGovernmentTypeNameWithNoTooltip('republic')] elects a new [ruler|e] every couple of years and keeping the same [ruler] over several [elections|e] will reduce our Republican Tradition. At low levels, it may collapse and revert to some kind of autocracy. For a well-functioning republic government, this measure should be kept high.

name: Devotion
description: Devotion represents the zeal of the [faith|e] inside our country. The higher it is, the more efficiently our [ShowGovernmentTypeName('theocracy')] will run.

name: Horde Unity
description: Horde Unity is a measure of how much support a $rank_kingdom_horde_ruler_suffix_male$ has from the tribes. It goes down over time and is increased by looting and razing provinces. A [ShowGovernmentTypeName('steppe_horde')] with low unity is likely to succumb to internal strife.

name: Tribal Cohesion
description: Tribal Cohesion is a measure of how aligned the members of our [ShowGovernmentTypeName('tribe')] are in terms of [religion|e] and [culture|e]. At low levels, running the [ShowGovernmentTypeNameWithNoTooltip('tribe')] will be like herding cats, with everyone wanting to do their own thing. This should be kept high for the [ShowGovernmentTypeNameWithNoTooltip('tribe')] to be run smoothly.

name: Government Power
description: This is the generic term for a measure of how well our [government|e] functions. There are several types: [legitimacy|e], [republican_tradition|e], [devotion|e], [horde_unity|e] and [tribal_cohesion|e].

name: Work of Art
description:
A work of art is something that an [artist|e] has created. When the art is created, it will directly increase the [cultural_influence|e] of the [primary_culture|e] of the [country|E] that the artist is working in. Art is present in a [location|e] but can be destroyed or captured if that location becomes [occupied|e] by any [enemy|e].
Having art in our [country] benefits our [prestige|e] and [cultural_tradition|e].

name: Art Quality
description:
The quality of the [works_of_art|e] impacts how much [prestige|e] and [cultural_tradition|e] it can provide.

A $game_concept_work_of_art$ can have the following levels of quality, from lowest to highest:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_bad$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_below_average$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_average$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_above_average$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_good$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_very_good$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_great$
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$ $art_quality_best$

name: Law
description: Each law has to have a [policy|e] selected for it, else it is not active. Different [government_types|e] and [religions|e] gain different laws, and more laws are given through [advances|e]. Depending on what [policy] we pick in a law, we will often impact our [societal_values|e].

name: Policy
description: Each [law|e] has one or more Policies to choose from. These determine how the law is handled in a [country|e].

name: Antagonism
description: Antagonism indicates how other [countries|e] are likely to view us, affecting their [opinion|e] of us. If they feel a lot of antagonism towards us, countries which consider us as relevant to their interests will be less inclined to engage in [diplomacy|e] and may act against our interests. Antagonism is caused by basic differences between countries' [societal_values|e], [government_types|e], [religion|e], [culture|e], and [language|e]. Some actions can also cause an antagonism 'bomb' in a [location|e] that affects the countries near it to varying degrees depending on how much they care about that location and about the antagonizing country. These antagonism 'bomb' effects will generally dissipate with time.

name: Antagonism Received
description: This is how much hostile diplomatic actions like [war|e] will impact our [antagonism|e].

name: Diplomacy
description:
Diplomacy is an interaction between two [countries|e] within [diplomatic_range|e] of each other. It is facilitated by [diplomats|e].

It covers everything from [alliances|e], [treaties|e], [subjects|e], and [overlords|e], and governs [war|e] and [peace|e].

High [prestige|e] makes it easier to do diplomacy, while high [antagonism|e] makes it harder.

name: Diplomatic Action
description: This is an action done by one [country|e] to another using [diplomats|e]. This includes forming [alliances|e], declaring [war|e] or many other things.

name: Diplomat
description: This represents how much [diplomacy|e] a [country|e] can do in a given time. Some [advances|e] or [societal_values|e] will increase this amount.

name: Diplomatic Limitation
description:
A [country|e] which is either a very dependent [subject|e] or a [junior_partner|e] in a [union|e] might be diplomatically limited. That means the following diplomatic actions are either not possible or heavily restricted:

$BULLET$ [ShowRelationTypeName('alliance')]
$BULLET$ [ShowRelationTypeName('food_access')]
$BULLET$ [ShowRelationTypeName('guarantee')]
$BULLET$ [ShowRelationTypeName('military_access')]
$BULLET$ [ShowRelationTypeName('fleet_basing_rights')]
$BULLET$ [ShowGenericActionName('create_building_subject')]
$BULLET$ [ShowGenericActionName('create_province_subject')]

Most subjects with limited diplomacy are incapable of declaring their own [wars|e] unless against very specific targets.

name: Bias
description: A bias is a certain attitude a [country|e] can have towards another one. It is split into three categories: [opinion|e], [trust|e] and [antagonism|e]. [country_interactions|e], [events|e] and historical setup have usually an impact on one of the three diplomatic aspects.

name: Opinion
description: This is how much a [country|e] likes or dislikes another [country]. The difference between [trust|e] and opinion is that a high opinion will stop a [country] from being hostile, but we would need trust to be able to work together.

name: Cultural Opinion
description: Every [culture|E] has a Cultural Opinion of every other Culture. This impacts the [opinion|e] a [country|e] with one [culture] has of a [country] of another [culture], and it also impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of a [pop|e].

name: Religious Opinion
description: Every [religion|E] has a Religious Opinion of every other [religion]. This impacts the [opinion|e] a [country|e] with one [religion] has of a [country] of another [religion], and it also impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of a [pop|e].

name: Rival
description:
[countries|e] can declare their hostility towards other countries by declaring them as $game_concept_rivals$. Countries have some additional hostile actions against their rivals, like the ability to fabricate a [casus_belli|e] and the option to intervene in their [wars|e].

A Rival $game_concept_country$ will not accept friendly [treaties|e] like [alliances|e], but [countries] with common rivals will have an easier time signing [treaties] between them.

Rivalry is not reciprocal, meaning that it is not necessary nor automatic for a $game_concept_country$ to rival back the ones that have rivaled it. A [country] that has declared another as its Rival is known as its [rival_enemy|e].

Only [countries] with similar [great_power_score|e] and not very good [opinion|e] can be declared Rivals, and the maximum number of $game_concept_rivals$ a [country] can have depends on its [country_rank|e].

name: Enemy
description: A [country|e] that has declared another a [rival|e] will be known as the Enemy of the latter. A [country] might have declared many [rivals], and yet have no Enemies, if no other [country] has rivalled them back.

name: Threat
description: This describes how worried a [country|e] is about another country. A more powerful neighbor will have a high threat level.

name: Royal Marriage
description: A royal marriage is a marriage between two [characters|e] from two different [countries|e], in an effort to tie them closer together, and give [prestige|e] to their [rulers|e].

name: Union
description: A union is a type of [treaty|e] that happens when two or more [countries|e] have come to have the same [ruler|e] due to [royal_marriages|e]. This functions like a defensive [alliance|e] in that they will come to each other's help automatically if they are attacked, but [laws|e] can be added to them to change how the union works. The most important member in the union is called the $game_concept_senior_partner$, while the rest of countries in a union are the $game_concept_junior_partners$.

name: Union Integration Level
description:
The $game_concept_union_integration_level$ describes how centralized the [personal_union|e] is through [laws|e] and [policies|e]. Every [member|e] which is present when a centralizing policy is implemented gets its level increased. With the final centralization policy, all $game_concept_junior_partners$ which have the same level as the $game_concept_union$ get unified by the $game_concept_senior_partner$.

Members which join the $game_concept_union$ later need to catch up their progress to be integrated via the [parliament|e].

name: Alliance
description: An alliance is a [treaty|e] between two [countries|e]. [countries] that are allied will not be able to declare [war|e] upon each other and can also be called to help in each other's [wars].

name: Alliance Bloc
description:
An alliance bloc is a coalition of [great_powers|e] and [regional_powers|e] bound together by [alliances|e]. The more powerful allies a [country|e] has, the higher its #Y alliance bloc saturation#!, which increases the [diplomatic_capacity|e] cost of each [alliance|e] it maintains.

A [great_power|e] ally contributes 1.0 to saturation; a [regional_power|e] ally contributes 0.5. These costs rise for every powerful [ally|e] added to the bloc, discouraging any single [country|e] from accumulating an overwhelming network of powerful [allies].

name: War Leader
description: A $game_concept_war_leader$ is one of the two [countries|e] who lead their respective side in a [war|e]. They will discuss the potential outcomes of the conflict by deciding over the [peace_treaties|e].

name: Call to Arms
description:
A call to arms is a [diplomatic_action|e] which can be done during [war|e] to every [ally|e] and other [countries|e] which have sworn to participate in military conflicts.

Countries that are the [war_defender|e] will automatically call their allies into the war, while countries that are the [war_attacker|e] have to manually call them, and it is more difficult for them to convince them to join.

name: Economic Support
description: This is a [treaty|e] where one [country|e] is sending [gold|e] each month to support the [finances|e] of the other [country]. This can often be the case when a country does not want to directly be involved in a [war|e] but still wants to support the effort.

name: War Reparations
description: This is a peace [treaty|e] where one [country|e] is made to send [GetDefine('NDiplomacy','WAR_REPARATIONS_FACTOR')|Y%0] of their income in [gold|e] each month to support the [finances|e] of the other [country], usually the victor, in retaliation for the war that just ended.

name: Treaty
description:
A Treaty is a signed diplomatic state of affairs between two or more [countries|e]. They could be for a limited time, or until further notice.
Treaties include [alliances|e], [military_access|e], [truce|e], and many more than can be created from [diplomacy|e].

name: Guarantee
description: This is a [treaty|e] where one [country|e] is guaranteeing the other [country], promising to protect them if they would be attacked in a [war|e].

name: Blocked Treaties
description: This makes it impossible for a [country|e] to sign any sort of [treaty|e] with the [country|e] they are blocked from doing it with.

name: Migration
description: [pops|e] will migrate from one [location|e] to another, if they feel that they would get a better life. Pops from some [estates|e] may not be allowed to migrate freely, depending on what [estate_privileges|e] that [country|e] may have enacted. Pops usually only migrate within the same [market|e], unless they are migrating to a [colonial_charter|e], or migrating due to an [event|e].

name: Migration Attraction
description: When [pops|e] live in a [location|e] with negative Migration Attraction, they will want to move to the [location] with the highest Migration Attraction in the same [market|e]. Some types of [pops|e] like [ShowPopTypeName('slaves')] are permanently restricted from migrating, while others like [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')] may only move if they are allowed to by their [estate_privileges|e].

name: Colonial Migration
description: [colonial_migration|e] is when [pops|e] [migrate|e] from the [core|e] [locations|e] to a [colonial_charter|e].

name: Average Satisfaction
description: This is the average [pop_satisfaction|e] in a [location|e]. This has a negative impact on the [prosperity|e] and the [control|e] of the location.

name: Separatism
description: [pops|e] that are not of the [primary_culture|e] will have a lower [pop_satisfaction|e] when they live in a [location|e] that has been conquered and not yet [integrated|e].

name: Population Growth
description: The Population Growth of the [pops|e] in a [location|e] is connected to how many are born in a month compared to how many died. A lack of [food|e], the spread of disease, a [siege|e], or other calamities may increase the number of people that die.

name: Pop Satisfaction
description:
This is how happy the [pop|e] is with its situation in life. It is influenced by the following factors:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[estate_satisfaction|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[unrest|e] of the [location|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$The [tolerance|e] of its [religion|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$If it is [accepted_culture|e] or not
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Access to [pop_needs|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$The [market_price|e] of the [pop_needs|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$The [cultural_opinion|e] of its [culture|e] by the [culture] of the [country|e]

name: Pop Needs
description:
A [pop_with_icon|e] has a list of [goods_with_icon|e] they need for their life, which depends on their [pop_type|e], [culture|e], [religion|e], and where they live. For instance, [ShowPopTypeName('nobles')] have much higher demands than the [lower_class|e]. If they cannot fulfill these needs, their [pop_satisfaction_with_icon|e] will suffer.

The amount of [goods] demanded by a [pop] increases with the [development_with_icon|e] of the [location|e] where they live.

name: Government Needs
description:
[government_needs] are those [goods|e] your [country|e] requires for [constructions|e] like [buildings|e], upgrading [location_rank|e], recruiting [armies|e] and [navies|e] or preparing [explorations|e].

[constructions|e] will stall if the [government_needs] cannot be satisfied in the [market|e] of the [location|e], so the fulfillment of [government_needs] should be a priority for any Government.

name: $MODIFIER_TYPE_NAME_global_peasant_enfranchisment$
description:
$MODIFIER_TYPE_DESC_global_peasant_enfranchisment$

Enfranchisement depends mostly on the [ShowSocietyDirectionName('free_subjects')] [societal_value_with_icon|e]. [towns_and_cities|e] have a higher level than [rural_locations|e], and some [buildings|e] can increase it or decrease it.

name: Estate Satisfaction
description:
This is how happy the [estate|e] is with how the [country|e] is currently being ruled. If this is high, the country will get some bonuses, but if it is low, it will give penalties, and if it is low enough, we will not be able to recruit [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e] from that [estate].

This also has a direct impact on the [pop_satisfaction|e] of the [pops|e] belong to this [estate].

name: Satisfaction Equilibrium
description: This is what the [estate_satisfaction|e] of an [estate|e] will move towards. The speed by which it moves depends on many factors.

name: Estate Tax Base
description: Each [estate|e] gains [gold|e] by a fraction of [tax_base|e] in each [location|e] that depends on their [estate_power|e] there compared to the other [estates]. This is then reduced by the [estate_enrichment|e].

name: Estate Power
description:
This is the power that an [estate|e] has in a [country|e]. It depends very much on the size of [population|e] of the [pop_types|e] that belong to the [estate], and what [estate_privileges|e] they have been given.

Some [pop_types|e] like [ShowPopTypeName('nobles')] get far more Estate Power per [pop|e] than [ShowPopTypeName('slaves')] do.

$BULLET_WITH_TAB$The total power of the [estates] reduces the [crown_power|e] of the [country].
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$The [tax_base|e] of a [location|e] is distributed depending on the size, Estate Power and [pop_type] of each pop there.

name: Crown Power
description:
This is the power that the crown has in a [country|e]. The bigger it is, the more powerful and efficient the [country] becomes. If too many [estate_privileges|e] have been given to the [estates|e], this may be so low that the country gets penalties.

There are [advances|e] through the [ages|e] that increase the [crown_power|e], especially as we advance into the [ShowAgeName('age_5_absolutism')].

name: Civil War
description: A civil war is a special type of [war|e] in which a [country|e] is at [war] not with another [country] but with a part of itself. It also differs from normal [wars] in that there is no [occupation|e] of [locations|e], but instead, they will switch [controller|e] immediately once they are [sieged|e].

name: White Peace
description: This is a [peace_treaty|e] that returns to the pre-war conditions.

name: Peace Treaty
description: This will be the conditions of a [peace_offer|e], which include the transfer of a [location|e] between two [countries|e], or a tribute in [gold|e] between them, or even some special treaties like [ShowPeaceTreatyTypeName('abandon_colonial_claim')], [ShowPeaceTreatyTypeName('execute_ruler')], or [ShowPeaceTreatyTypeName('peace_humiliate')].

name: Peace Offer
description:
It is a diplomatic action that puts an end to an ongoing [war|e] between two or more [countries|e]. In it, one side will be able to state their conditions to the other side as [peace_treaties|e]. Once the other side accepts them, the peace will be signed and the [war] will end.

How much a [country] will be able to get out of a peace treaty will depend on its [war_score].

name: Peace Offer value
description: This is how much a [peace_treaty|e] will cost to add to a [peace_offer|e]. It is usually compared to the [war_score|e] to determine whether the other [country|e] would accept it or not.

name: Peace
description: Peace is the status in which the [country|e] is not in any ongoing [war|e].

name: Unconditional Surrender
description: Upon offering unconditional surrender, all of the currently unoccupied [locations|e]] will fall under enemy control and the enemy will gain 100% [war_score|e]. [armies|e] of the [country|e] that surrendered will become [exiled|e] and unable to fight in future [battles|e] until [peace|e] is signed. The recipient of an unconditional surrender will be alerted of the enemy's surrender and from then on will be able to enforce any possible peace up to 100% warscore cost. If the recipient country does not sign peace after a couple of months, they will get a call for peace giving them monthly [war_exhaustion|e] which increases faster than normal. The peace will be automatically accepted by the country that surrendered. When naturally reaching 100% warscore, the AI will usually unconditionally surrender. There are also some other cases in which the AI unconditionally surrenders.

name: War
description:
A war is created when one [country|e] uses a [diplomat|e] on another country to start a conflict. Countries that are [allied|e] with either side may get called into the war.

During a war, [armies|e] and [navies|e] from each side that encounter each other will [battle|e] each other. [armies] will be able to [siege|e] the [enemies|e] [locations|e], while [navies|e] can [blockade|e] their [ports|e].

A war continue until a [peace_treaty|e] is signed, and [peace|e] reigns again between the involved [countries].

name: Attacker
description:
In a [war_with_icon|e], the Attacker is the side whose leader initiated the conflict and chose the [casus_belli_with_icon|e].

In order to earn [war_score_with_icon|e], the Attacker side needs to fulfil the [war_goal_with_icon|e].

name: Defender
description:
In a [war_with_icon|e], the Defender is the side whose leader was declared war upon. The Defender side will automatically call their [allies_with_icon|e] into the [war].

In order to earn [war_score_with_icon|e], the Defender side needs to prevent the [war_attacker|e] from fulfilling the [war_goal_with_icon|e].

name: War Participation
description: This is how much a [country|e] has contributed to the progress of the [war|e]. This is primarily done through [battles|e], [blockades|e] and [sieges|e].

name: Warscore
description: Warscore is the value that indicates how well a [country|e] is performing in a specific [war|e]. A [country] can increase their warscore by winning [battles|e], managing to [siege|e] [enemy|e] [locations|e], achieving the [war_goal|e], and establishing [blockades|e].

name: Wargoal
description: A wargoal is the objective established for a certain [war|e], and it will depend on the type of [casus_belli|e] used. Achieving the wargoal will give a considerable amount of [war_score|e].

name: Co-belligerent
description:
A [country|e] that is called into a [war|e] as a $game_concept_cobelligerent$ will be able to call its own [allies|e] into the [war].

Taking [locations|e] from a $game_concept_cobelligerent$ [country] in a [peace_treaty|e] will have the same cost as the war leader's.

name: Casus Belli
description: Literally meaning #italic Cause for War#!, it is the justification a [country|e] uses for starting a [war|e]. Depending on the Casus Belli used, the type of [war] and the [war_goal|e] will be different.

name: Core
description:
A [location|e] that is a Core of a [country|e] is the integral part of that [country].
If that [location] is ever lost in a [war|e], it is easy to fabricate a [casus_belli|e] to attempt to get it back.
Any [integrated|e] [location] who has a majority of the [owner_s|e] [primary_culture|e] or any [accepted_culture|e] will become a Core.
Cores gained through [effects|e] or those lost to other countries will disappear after [GetDefine('NCountry', 'SCRIPTED_CORE_DURATION_YEARS')] years if they do not have the correct [culture|e].

name: Stockpile
description: This is the quantity of the [good|e] that is currently stored in warehouses in the [market|e]. It increases if [supply|e] is higher than [demand|e], but will decrease if the opposite. [buildings|e], [constructions|e], [units|e], and [pops|e] in the market will use the stockpile for their needs.

name: Effective Supply
description: This is based on the [supply|e] of a [good|e] in a [market|e] but the impact of [imports|e] is reduced.

name: Effective Demand
description: This is based on the [demand|e] of a [good|e] in a [market|e] but the impact of [exports|e] is reduced.

name: Supply
description: This is the quantity of the [good|e] that is produced from [buildings|e], gathered as [raw_materials|e], or [imported|e] into the [market|e].

name: Demand
description: This is the quantity of the [good|e] that [buildings|e] need for their input, how much the [pops|e] need for their lives, how much various [constructions|e] require, and how much [exports|e] are requested from a [market|e].

name: Market Balance
description: The $game_concept_market_balance$ of a [good|e] is the difference between the [supply_with_icon|e] and the [demand_with_icon|e] of that [good] inside a [market_with_icon|e].

name: Market Value
description: This is the aggregated value of all monthly transactions in a [market|e]. It serves as an estimation of its total wealth.

name: Price Stability
description: Price Stability is determined by the current [age|e] and decides how much the [target_price|e] is affected by [supply|e] and [demand|e].

name: Target Price
description:
Target Price is determined by [supply|e], [demand|e], and [price_stability|e].
As a proportion of the base price, it will scale between [price_stability] at overwhelming supply; and 1 / [price_stability] at overwhelming demand.

name: Price Impact
description: The [market_price|e] of the [goods|e] that is the [pop_needs|e] of a [pop|e] has a direct impact of its [pop_satisfaction|e].

name: Market Price
description:
The price at which a certain [good|e] is traded at the [market_center|e].
The market price is incrementally adjusted towards the [target_price|e].
The [sell_price|E] in other locations may differ from the market price, based on [market_access|e].

name: Export Market
description: This is the [market|e] where the [goods|e] of a trade are bought, creating an [export|e].

name: Import Market
description: This is the [market|e] where the [goods|e] of a trade are sold, creating an [import|e].

name: Market
description:
A Market is where [goods|e] are bought and sold.
It is based in a [market_center|e], but includes other locations based on their [market_access|e] and [protectionism|e].
All these locations will exclusively buy from and sell to this market's [stockpile|e].

[markets] are color-coded depending on how relevant they are to you:

Depending on your relation with them, [markets] can be [domestic_markets], [trading_markets], [foreign_markets], or [distant_markets].

name: Domestic Market
description:
A $game_concept_domestic_market$ is a [market_with_icon|e] in which you own [locations_with_icon|e]. Your [locations] depend on their [market] to buy all the stuff they need, be it for government [construction_with_icon|e], [buildings_with_icon|e], [pop_needs_with_icon|e], or [food_with_icon|e].

Ensuring the supply of [goods] in your $game_concept_domestic_markets$ is paramount for the running of your [country], since you might not be able to build [buildings] or recruit [regiments|e] if the necessary [goods] are missing.

name: Trading Market
description:
A $game_concept_trading_market$ is a [market_with_icon|e] in which you do not [own|e] any territory, but have [merchant_capacity_with_icon|e] from your [foreign_buildings_with_icon|e].

This means that you do not necessarily care about the [good_with_icon|e] needs of that [market], its [food|e] supply, or its [population|e], but you can use your [merchant_capacity] there to make profit, or to supply your [domestic_markets_with_icon|e].

name: Foreign Market
description: A $game_concept_foreign_market$ is a [market_with_icon|e] in which you do not [own|e] any territory, nor have any [merchant_capacity_with_icon|e]. That means you cannot conduct [trade_with_icon|e] from them, but you can still trade with them using your [merchant_capacity] in other [markets] within [trade_range_with_icon|e].

name: Distant Market
description: A $game_concept_distant_market$ is a [market_with_icon|e] that lies beyond the [trade_range_with_icon|e] of all of your [domestic_markets_with_icon|e], so you cannot conduct any [trade_with_icon|e] with them.

name: Market Center
description: The [location|e] that a [market|e] is centered upon. The [owner|e] of this location gets some benefits from it, but most importantly, they can control who can have access to this market.

name: Market Owner
description: The Market Owner of a [market|e] is the [country|e] that [owns|e] its [market_center|e]. The Market Owner can destroy or relocate the [market], and prevent other [countries] from trading in it.

name: Market Attraction
description:
This impacts how much pull a [market_center|e] has over a [location|e] to make it a part of its [market|e].

It is countered by [protectionism|e].

name: Market Protection
description:
$MODIFIER_TYPE_DESC_local_trade_protection_factor$

Market Protection increases mainly with the [control|e] of the [location].

name: Counterespionage
description: Counterespionage is how good a [country|e] is to actively stop the build up of [foreign|e] [spy_networks|e] in their country.

name: Spy Network
description: This describes the extent to which a [country|e] has infiltrated another with a network of informants, double agents, and general turncoats, and thus how much inside knowledge they have of that country. It can be used to perform a variety of insidious diplomatic actions.

name: Intelligence Fog
description: Some information about foreign [countries|e] and their [locations|e] is hidden unless you have a sufficient [spy_network|e] in that country. Building a stronger spy network reveals more detailed data, including [population|e] composition, economic output, military strength, and more.

name: Favors
description:
Favors represent how much one [country|e] has promised, or otherwise owes, to another [country].
Favors can be spent to ask the other [country] to do something. If favors get too unbalanced, refusing to do these things can cause a loss of [trust|e] or even [diplomatic_reputation|e].

name: Trust
description:
Trust represents how likely one [country|e] finds it that another [country] will act honorably towards them.
Whether friend or foe, Trust is a crucial component in forging lasting agreements.

name: Trust Equilibrium
description: Trust equilibrium represents the amount [trust|e] with another [country] will drift towards. Trust is a crucial component in forging lasting agreements.

name: Support Rebels
description: This is when a [country|e] decides to offer assistance to a group of [rebels|e] in a different [country], with the hope that if the [rebels] are victorious then the new government in place will be friendly towards them.

name: Great Power
description:
A [great_power] is a [country|e] that has accumulated enough [great_power_points|e] by dominating areas of high economic value to project its influence across the world.

A [country] dominates an [area|e] when it controls at least two-thirds of the area's ownable [locations|e], counting [subjects|e] at a reduced rate. Each area is worth 1–10 [great_power_points|e] depending on its potential tax base relative to the world median.

Once a [country] crosses the [great_power_points|e] threshold it gains extra [diplomatic_capacity|e], [diplomats|e], [power_projection|e], [prestige|e], and [ShowModifierTypeName('mercenary_range')], as well as the ability to #T Enforce Peace, Intervene in Wars, and Threaten War#! anywhere in the world.

name: Regional Power
description:
A [regional_power] is a [country|e] that has accumulated enough [great_power_points|e] to dominate its region but has not yet reached [great_power|e] status.

A [regional_power] earns half the bonuses of a [great_power] — extra [diplomatic_capacity|e], [diplomats|e], [power_projection|e], [prestige|e], and [ShowModifierTypeName('mercenary_range')] — but its #T Enforce Peace, Intervene in Wars, and Threaten War#! anywhere in the world actions are limited to [countries|e] whose capital lies in an adjacent [region|e].

name: Normal Power
description: A [normal_power] is a [country|e] that is not a [great_power|e].

name: Hegemony
description:
Hegemony is established in different fields, where the [great_power|e] with the greatest level in each field will be proclaimed to be the Hegemon, earning some nice bonuses.
[ShowDatabase('hegemony')]

name: Tier
description: This is the name for the level that a [formable_country|e] has. Every [country|e] belongs to a Tier from I to IV, depending on how hard the formation requirements are. Most importantly, [countries] can only form countries of higher Tiers than their current one.

name: Country Rank
description:
$game_concept_country_rank_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabaseWithIcon('country_rank')]

name: Country Type
description: The $game_concept_country_type$ defines the condition of existence of a [country|e] and has enormous gameplay implications. Some $game_concept_countries$ are defined by the [locations|e] they [own|e] and cannot exist without them, while others are defined by their [armies|e], their [buildings|e], or their [pops|e].

name: Diplomatic Range
description: Diplomatic Range limits the physical distance our diplomats can travel to conduct diplomacy. The distance to be traveled is from one capital to the other.

name: Diplomatic Capacity
description:
An alliance with everyone is an alliance with no one. A [country|e] that maintains more relations than its $game_concept_diplomatic_capacity$ will suffer a penalty to their [diplomatic_reputation|e] and [prestige|e]. Certain [subject_types|e] possess a $game_concept_diplomatic_upkeep$ which reduces the available capacity too.

Membership in some [international_organizations|e] will cost some $game_concept_diplomatic_capacity$, and the power of your [ally|e] determines the cost of an [alliance|e].

name: Diplomatic Reputation
description: A [country|e]'s Diplomatic Reputation represents how highly regarded it is in international relations. In particular, it affects how [trusted|e] it is by all other countries.

name: Trade Range
description:
Defines how far a [country|e] can trade without extra cost. Routes within $game_concept_trade_range$ have no additional transport penalty. Routes that exceed it remain possible, but transport costs increase with the distance beyond the range limit.

A larger $game_concept_trade_range$ makes long-haul routes — such as colonial goods from the New World or spices from Asia — more affordable by pushing more of each route into the free zone.

$game_concept_trade_range$ can be increased primarily through [advances|e], although some [laws|e], [privileges|e] and [reforms|e] may affect it too.

name: Naval Range
description: This is simply how far our [ships|e] can [explore|e] before they need to turn back for more supplies.

name: Colonial Range
description: This is simply how far away we can [colonize|e].

name: Military Access
description: Military Access allows our troops to move through the land of the other [countries|e].

name: Fleet Basing Rights
description: Fleet basing rights allow one country's [ports|e] to be used by another country's [ships|e], thus extending the range that they can explore and allowing them to [repair|e] away from home.

name: Mothballed
description: Mothballed [ships|e] require little [gold|e] to maintain them but are not kept in a [combat|e] ready state, so can be defeated much more easily.

name: Country Interaction
description:
These are the [actions|e] we can do with a [country|e]. This is either through [diplomacy|e] or by interacting with a [subject|e].

Examples include [ShowCountryInteractionName('sabotage_reputation')], [ShowCountryInteractionName('pay_off_debt')] or [ShowCountryInteractionName('give_location_to_subject')].

name: Relation Type
description:
These are relations we can form with a [country|e]. This is either through [diplomacy|e] or by interacting with a [subject|e].

Examples include [ShowRelationTypeName('embargo_nation')], [ShowRelationTypeName('sound_toll_exemption')] or [ShowRelationTypeName('scutage')].

name: Subsistence Agriculture
description: [rgo_pops|e] that are not employed in an [rgo|e] or a [building|e] work in $game_concept_subsistence_agriculture$. They will generate food in smaller quantities than $game_concept_resource_gathering_operations$ working [food_raw_materials|e], often barely enough to cater for their own needs. All [unemployed|e] population is assumed to be doing this simpler form of gathering of [food|e] even if the [location|e] has a [raw_material|e] which is not directly related to [food|e].

name: Regular Regiment
description: Regular Regiments are recruited manually by a [country|e] using most commonly [manpower|e] and [gold|e]. These form the standing [armies|e], and are rather limited in numbers until you get the [advances|e] from later [ages|e].

name: Levy Combat Efficiency
description: This impacts how effective will a [regiment|e] of [levies|e] perform in [combat|e] compared to a [regular_regiment|e].

name: Levy
description: A levy is a military unit that a [pop|e] will raise when called. It is either an [army_levy|e] or a [navy_levy|e].

name: Army Levy
description:
An army levy is a [regiment|e] that has been raised directly from [pops|e]. When the unit is recruited, the [pops] they get recruited from are reduced, and when the unit is disbanded, any survivors return to the [pops]. These people are less trained than a regular [army|e] recruited from [manpower|e], and they do not reinforce.

A levy [regiment|e] also has the following effect:

[ShowModifierEffect('is_army_levy')]

name: Naval Levy
description:
A naval levy is a transport [ship|e] that has been commandeered directly from [pops|e]. When the unit is recruited, the [pops] that own the ship and their crew are taken from [pops] in [locations|e], and when the unit is disbanded, any survivors return to the [pops]. These ships are generally flimsier than a [navy|e] recruited from [sailors|e], and should be guarded by proper ships with cannons.

A levy [ship|e] also has the following effect:

[ShowModifierEffect('is_navy_levy')]

name: Mercenary
description:
Mercenaries are private individuals who take part in military conflict for [gold|e], but are otherwise outsiders to the conflict. A [country|e]'s own units can be hired out to other countries as mercenaries.

The base cost of $game_concept_mercenaries$ is 50% higher than [regulars|e].

name: Hiring Fee
description: This is the upfront cost of hiring this mercenary company, notwithstanding the [mercenary_contract_length|e].

name: Monthly Fee
description: This is the monthly cost of hiring this company. It depends mostly on the number and the quality of its [regiments|e], as well as the [abilities|e] of its [commander|e].

name: Contract Length
description: This is the amount of months that this company will serve at the behest of its contractor.

name: Weather System
description: These are weather patterns that can bring high winds, rain, snow and sandstorms to [locations|e] around the world, occasionally wreaking havoc.

name: Prisoner
description: Prisoners are enemy [regiments|e] that have been captured after a battle. They can be bribed to be [mercenaries|e] fighting for their captors, ransomed, or simply disposed of...humanely or not.

name: Privateer Maintenance
description: While [privateers|e] can enrich themselves, they still need to be supported by a [country|e] when it comes to [sailors|e].

name: Privateer Durability
description: [privateers|e] can be damaged and destroyed by [anti_piracy_warfare|e] in their [area|e]. With a higher Privateer Durability, they can survive for longer.

name: Privateer
description: Privateers are enterprising people who have responded to the call from a [country|e] to wreak havoc on the [maritime_presence|e] of anyone potentially [hostile|e]. For those that encounter them, they are indistinguishable from [pirates|e].

name: Pirate
description: Pirates are boat-based attackers of other [ships|e] or coastal areas who steal [goods|e] or [gold|e].

name: Colonial Charter
description:
A colonial charter is formed by a [country|e] that wishes to [colonize|e] an entire [province|e].
The Colonial Charter will [migrate|e] [pops|e] to the [province]. When the [location|e] is [fully_settled|e] the [location] will become [owned|e] by the colonizer.

name: Colonized
description: A colony is when a [country|e] has a [colonial_charter|e] in a [province|e] that slowly sends their own [population|e] there to become the new majority.

name: Fully Settled
description: When there is at least #G 1,000#! [pops|e] living in a [location|e] and enough of the [pops|e] in the [location] in the [colonial_charter|e] is the [primary_or_accepted_culture|e] and official [primary_religion|e] of the owner of the charter, the location is considered Fully Settled. The percentage required is based on the [power_projection|e].

name: Laborers or Slaves
description:
These are the [pop_types|e] that can work gathering [raw_materials|e].

$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('laborers')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowPopTypeName('slaves')]

name: Plantation
description:
These are specific [buildings|e] that need to be built to exploit some specific types of [raw_materials|e] like [ShowGoodsName('cotton')], [ShowGoodsName('sugar')], and [ShowGoodsName('tobacco')].

For these buildings we would specifically need [ShowPopTypeName('slaves')].

name: Friend
description: A friendly [country|e] is one who is either our [subject|e], our [overlord|e], or a [war_ally|e]. Of course, our own country is also considered friendly.

name: Unrest
description: It is a value that negatively impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of the [pops|e] in a certain [location|e].

name: Hostile
description: A hostile [country|e] is one that wants to do us harm, such as [rebels|e], [pirates|e], or a country we are at [war|e] with.

name: War Enemy
description:
Two [countries|e] that are at [war|e] against each other will view each other as enemies, and they will [battle|e] when their [armies|e] or [navies|e] meet.

[rebels|e] and [pirates|e] are enemies to all.

name: Situation
description:
A Situation is what the game uses for the most important historical incidents that involve more than one [country|e], and/or are happening over a period of time.

Some of the most important Situations include the [ShowSituationName('black_death')] and [ShowSituationName('reformation')].

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_1_traditions')]:
$BULLET$Hundred Years' War
$BULLET$Guelphs and Ghibellines
$BULLET$Rise of the Turks
$BULLET$Nanbokuchō Jidai
$BULLET$Fall of Delhi

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_2_renaissance')]:
$BULLET$Black Death
$BULLET$Hussite Wars
$BULLET$Red Turban Rebellions
$BULLET$Rise of $name_timur$
$BULLET$Western Schism

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_3_discovery')]:
$BULLET$Great Pestilence
$BULLET$Italian Wars
$BULLET$The Reformation
$BULLET$Sengoku Jidai
$BULLET$Treaty of Tordesillas

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_4_reformation')]:
$BULLET$Council of Trent
$BULLET$War of Religions

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_5_absolutism')]:
$BULLET$Columbian Exchange
$BULLET$Golden Age of Piracy
$BULLET$Little Ice Age

The Situations of the [ShowAgeName('age_6_revolutions')]:
$BULLET$Colonial Revolution
$BULLET$People's Uprising

name: Situation Action
description:
These are the [actions|e] we can do while a certain [situation|e] is active. They vanish once the situation is resolved.

Some examples are [ShowGenericActionName('hide_from_black_death')] and [ShowGenericActionName('rtr_rekindle_revolt')].

name: Tension
description:
Measures how inflamed the [ShowSituationName('italian_wars')] have become. It rises passively each month and faster when League leaders are actively at war. Higher Tension makes all League leaders more aggressive and shortens the time between their wars.

Tension drops significantly when a League is dissolved via a peace deal.

name: Disaster
description:
A Disaster is an important and disruptive incident affecting a single [country|e], and they could last or remain active over a long period of time, until the country manages to overcome it.

Some of the most important Disasters include [ShowDisasterName('ambrosian_republic_disaster')] and [ShowDisasterName('dissolution_of_delhi')].

name: Tolerance
description:
Tolerance represents how respectfully the population of a certain [religion|e] is treated in a society. Every [country|e] has a different $game_concept_tolerance$ value towards its [primary_religion|e], towards [heretics|e], and towards [heathens|e].

A positive $game_concept_tolerance$ value increases the [pop_satisfaction|e] of [pops|e], as well as the [diplomatic_opinion|e] towards $game_concept_countries$ of that $game_concept_religion$. Reversely, a negative $game_concept_tolerance$ increases [unrest|e] and lowers $game_concept_diplomatic_opinions$.

name: Minor Revolt
description:
If a [rebel_movement|e] has not managed to garner enough support when it reaches #W 100%#!, it will not break away in open [revolt|e], but cause a [ShowModifier('minor_rebel_uprising')] in the affected [locations|e], with the following penalties:

[ShowModifierEffect('minor_rebel_uprising')].

name: Revolter
description: A revolt is when a group of [locations|e] break away as a new [country|e] and start a [war|e] against the original [owner|e].

name: Rebel Movement
description:
A Rebel Movement is a group of [pops|e] that band together against their government due to their low [pop_satisfaction].

There are various types of Rebel Movements. For instance, [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] will attempt a [revolt|e], while an unhappy [estate|e] will try to start a [civil_war|e].

name: Estate Rebels
description: Rebels is a faction that are either [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] that is attempting a [revolt|e] or an unhappy [estate|e] that is trying to force a [civil_war|e].

name: Nationalist Rebels
description: Rebels is a faction that are either [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] that is attempting a [revolt|e] or an unhappy [estate|e] that is trying to force a [civil_war|e].

name: Pretender Rebels
description: Rebels is a faction that are either [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] that is attempting a [revolt|e] or an unhappy [estate|e] that is trying to force a [civil_war|e].

name: Religious Rebels
description: Rebels is a faction that are either [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] that is attempting a [revolt|e] or an unhappy [estate|e] that is trying to force a [civil_war|e].

name: Slave Rebels
description: Rebels is a faction that are either [pops|e] of another [culture|e] or [religion|e] that is attempting a [revolt|e] or an unhappy [estate|e] that is trying to force a [civil_war|e].

name: Disloyal Subjects
description:
When a [subject] has less than [GetDefine('NDiplomacy','TOO_DISLOYAL_THRESHOLD')] [subject_loyalty|e] towards its [overlord|e], it becomes a Disloyal Subject.

When in such a state, it will no longer help in the [wars|e] of its [overlord] and cannot be [annexed|e].

name: Loyal Subjects
description:
When a [subject] has more than [GetDefine('NDiplomacy','TOO_DISLOYAL_THRESHOLD')] [subject_loyalty|e] towards its [overlord|e], it becomes a Loyal Subject.

When in such a state, it will join the [wars|e] of its [overlord] and may be [annexed|e].

name: Truce
description: A truce is automatically created when a [peace_treaty|e] is signed between two [countries|e]. Declaring [war|e] on someone we have a truce with will have severe penalties. Some diplomatic actions may be entirely blocked with nations we have a truce with.

name: Trait
description: $game_concept_trait_upper_desc$

name: Ruler Trait
description:
A $game_concept_ruler_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is either [ruler|e] or [regent|e].

A $game_concept_character$ can earn up to three $game_concept_ruler_traits$ while ruling a [country|e].

name: Health Trait
description:
A $game_concept_health_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that reflects the health (or unhealth) of a [character|e].

A $game_concept_character$ can end up with any number of $game_concept_health_traits$ throughout their life.

They can be received from various sources, such as [events|e], [diseases|e], or [battle|e]. They may even be saddled with a $game_concept_health_trait$ from birth.

$game_concept_traits$ borne of $game_concept_battle$ increase in their likliness depending on the number of friendly casualties.

name: General Trait
description:
A $game_concept_general_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is a [general|e].

A $game_concept_character$ can earn up to one $game_concept_general_trait$ while fighting land [battles|e].

name: Admiral Trait
description:
An $game_concept_admiral_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is an [admiral|e].

A $game_concept_character$ can earn up to one $game_concept_admiral_trait$ while fighting naval [battles|e].

name: Artist Trait
description:
An $game_concept_artist_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is an [artist|e].

Every $game_concept_artist$ has its trait assigned when they are created as a $game_concept_character$.

name: Explorer Trait
description:
An $game_concept_explorer_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is an [explorer|e].

A $game_concept_character$ can earn up to one $game_concept_explorer_trait$ while leading [exploration|e] missions.

name: Child Trait
description: Every [child|e] and [adolescent|e] has one single $game_concept_child_trait$ while growing up, which is removed once they become an [adult|e]. $game_concept_child_traits$ influence the rate at which they increase their [abilities|e].

name: Religious Figure Trait
description:
A $game_concept_religious_figure_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is a [religious_figure|e].

A $game_concept_character$ with a $game_concept_religious_figure_trait$ can give a boost to the [country|e] that employs them.

name: Cabinet Trait
description:
A $game_concept_cabinet_trait$ is a type of [trait|e] that is only active while a [character|e] is a [cabinet_member|e].

A $game_concept_character$ with a $game_concept_cabinet_trait$ can give a boost to the [country|e] that employs them.

The effects of a $game_concept_cabinet_trait$ are doubled if the Character is promoted to [head_of_the_cabinet|e].

name: Role
description:
$game_concept_roles$ are different positions that an [adult|e] [character|e] may fulfill in a [country|e]. The [abilities|e] of a $game_concept_character$ will have different effects depending on their Role, and they will be able to earn different [traits|e].

Normally a $game_concept_character$ may only perform one Role at a time, but sometimes [rulers|e] and [regents|e] can act as [generals|e] or [admirals|e].

name: Commander
description: A Commander is an [admiral|e] or [general|e] in charge of a [unit|e].

name: General
description: This is a [character|e] that has been assigned the role of leading an [army|e].

name: Admiral
description: This is a [character|e] that has been assigned the role of leading a [navy|e].

name: Regent
description: This is a [character|e] that is acting as the [ruler|e] of the [country|e] during a [regency|e].

name: Artistic Skill
description: This skill is the biggest influence on the [art_quality|e] of the [work_of_art|e] that an [artist|e] can create.

name: Artist Salary
description: The amount of [gold|e] an [artist|e] will earn.

name: Trade Route Maintenance
description:
This represents the cost of establishing [trades|e] between [markets|e]. Trading is not free, as the ships, wagons, and caravans need to be maintained, and the merchants themselves need to be paid.

Trade Maintenance increases with distance, and is affected by the existence of [sound_tolls|e].

name: Trade Advantage
description:
The $game_concept_merchant_power$ of [countries|e] in a [market|e] determines who will be able to get their [exports|e] fulfilled first.

If there is a limited amount of [supply|e] of [goods|e] in a $game_concept_market$ they get distributed by the $game_concept_merchant_power$ that each [country|e] has in that $game_concept_market$.

name: Trade Capacity
description:
This represents how much a [country|e] can [export|e] and/or [import|e] from a [market|e].

Each [trade|e] created from this [market] uses [merchant_capacity] depending on the distance to the other [market], and the volume of [goods|e] that [trade] is doing.

name: Transport Capacity
description: Transport capacity simply describes how many men, or [strength|e], from [regiments|e] we can get on our [ship|e].

name: Food Storage
description: This is the amount of [food|e] that a [regiment|e] or [ship|e] can carry with them.

name: Daily Food Consumption
description: This is how much [food|e] a [regiment|e] will consume each day.

name: Starving
description:
When a [province|e] has no [food|e] left in the [provincial_food|e], the [pops|e] will starve and die.

This gives the following effect:
[ShowModifierEffect('province_starving')]

name: Market Food
description:
Every [province|e] will either [buy_food|e] or [sell_food|e] in the [market|e] they belong to, at a price that depends on the amount of $game_concept_food$ stored in the $game_concept_market$ [stockpile|e]. The [owner|e] of the $game_concept_province$ will be the one affected by the cost or profit of the transaction, meaning that $game_concept_provinces$ with a surplus of $game_concept_food$ will add to the [income|e] of the $game_concept_owner$, while deficits will result in [expenses|e].

You can create [trades|e] of [food_raw_materials|e] to move $game_concept_food$ between $game_concept_markets$.

name: Distributing Food
description: This will send [food|e] from the [navy|e] to any [army|e] in an adjacent [location|e] that can not get [food] from its current [location] or a nearby [supply_depot|e].

name: Gathering Food
description: A [navy|e] that is Gathering Food will take [food|e] from all adjacent [locations|e] it has [food_access|e] to, to fill its [food_capacity|e]. The [navy] can then [distribute_food|e] when needed.

name: Food Access
description: Food Access allows our [armies|e] and [navies|e] to gather [food|e] from the [locations|e] of the other [countries|e].

name: Buying Food
description:
When a [province|e] has a low amount of [food|e], they will buy more at their local [market|e]. This is only possible if the province is not under [siege|e].

A [province] can only buy each month as much [food|e] at once as the total capacity of the [food_stockpile|e] of the [province].

name: Selling Food
description:
When a [province|e] has a surplus of [food|e] and can not store any more of it, they will sell it at their local [market|e]. This is only possible if the province is not under [siege|e].

A [province] can only buy each month as much [food|e] at once as the total capacity of the [food_stockpile|e] of the [province].

name: Hull Size
description: The larger the hull size, the less damage a [ship|e] takes in [combat|e].

name: Annexation
description:
When an [overlord|e] completely takes over one of its [subjects|e].

The [overlord] will gain all of the [subject]'s [owned|e] [locations|e], [cores|e], and [characters|e]. The [subject|e] will no longer exist as a [country|e].

The subject can slow the progress with the [ShowCabinetActionName('frustrate_annexation')] [cabinet_action|e], or declare [war|e] with their special [ShowCasusBelliName('cb_resist_annexation')] [casus_belli|e].

A [disloyal_subject|e] cannot be annexed.

name: Cannons
description: The more cannons a [ship|e] has, the more damage they can do in [combat|e].

name: Flanking Ability
description: This determines how much damage it can inflict on units in a different [section|e] in combat.

name: Secure Flanks
description: This provides a defensive bonus when there are [friendly|e] troops in a neighboring [section|e]. If both flanks are secure, the bonus is doubled.

name: Anti-Piracy Impact
description: This is the effect the [ship|e] will have on [privateers|e] in their area.

name: Combat Power
description: This is the direct damage dealing attribute of a [regiment|e] in [combat|e]. It is multiplied with the [strength|e] of the [regiment] to determine how much damage the [regiment] does.

name: Bombard Efficiency
description: This is the chance that artillery [regiments|e] have to fire during the [bombard_phase|e].

name: Frontage
description: In a [combat|e], only a limited amount of [regiments|e] or [ships|e] can fight at the same time, and this is called frontage. Some [locations|e] with harsher [topography|e] or [vegetation|e] may reduce the frontage further. There are also some types of [sub_units|e] that may use less frontage than others, and some that may use more frontage.

name: Initiative
description:
Initiative is the chance that a [regiment|e] will [engage|e] during the [combat_phase|e] of [combat|e].

Every hour, assuming there is enough [frontage|e] available, all the [regiments] not currently [engaged] will attempt to join the fray.

The chance is calculated as (Initiative * [GetDefine('NCombat','INITIATIVE_CHANCE_EACH')]) + ([GetDefine('NCombat','INITIATIVE_CHANCE_EACH')] * number of hours in combat); if the chance is higher than a [d100|e], then the [regiment] becomes [engaged] in the fighting.

In general, light and ranged [regiments|e] have the highest Initiative.

name: Combat Speed
description: This is the ability to move from the [reserves|e] to any other [section|e] inside a [battle|e]. For [ships|e] it also impacts how quickly a damaged one can leave the current [section|e] to retreat.

name: Blockade Capacity
description: This determines how good a [ship|e] is at blockading. This is directly compared to a value in the target [location|e] depending on its [development|e], [population|e], [imports|e], and [exports|e] it has.

name: Crew Size
description: This determines how many [sailors|e] are required for the [ship|e] to be operational.

name: Total Strength
description: This how many men an [army|e] has in total, adding together all the individual [strength|e] of each [regiment|e].

name: Strength
description: This how many men a [regiment|e] currently has.

name: Maximum Strength
description: This increases how many more men a [regiment|e] has, thus increasing its [manpower|e] cost. A [regiment] with a higher amount of [manpower], but with the same [frontage|e], is more effective in [combat|e].

name: Attrition Loss
description: How much damage [attrition|e] does to a [regiment|e] or [ship|e] each month.

name: Attrition
description:
Attrition is applied at the start of each month, which for [regiments|e] means that people die, while for [ships|e] it also damages the actual ship. Some attrition is [non_avoidable_attrition|e] and the main sources for attrition include the following:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[army|e] without [food|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Total [unit_weight|e] in [location|e] above [supply_limit|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[winter|e], [topography|e], [vegetation|e], or [climate|e]

name: Unavoidable Attrition
description: Usually [armies|e] do not take [attrition|e] if they are within the [zone_of_control|e] of a [fort|e] owned and controlled by themselves, their direct [subjects|e], or their direct [overlord|e], but some things like the [ShowSituationName('black_death')] can not be avoided like that.

name: Supply Limit
description: This is the maximum [unit_weight|e] that a [location|e] can supply without causing additional [food_consumption|e] to the [army|e].

name: Unit Weight
description:
This is an accumulated value that depends on the current [strength|e] of the [regiment|e] and which [unit_type|e] it is.
This is compared directly to the [supply_limit|e] in the current [location|e] when calculating [attrition|e].

name: Naval Damage
description: This impacts how much damage [ships|e] can take or do during [combat|e].

name: Damage Taken
description: During a [battle|e], a [regiment|e] or [ship|e] will take damage both to their [morale|e] and [strength|e]. The amount depends on the [combat_power|e], [strength|e], and other statistics of the enemy, while attributes like [experience|e], [strength_damage_taken|e], or [morale_damage_taken|e] can reduce it.

name: Strength Damage Taken
description: This impacts the amount of damage a unit takes in [combat|e]. For [ships|e], it is the damage to the actual [ship|e], while for [regiments|e] this determines how much [manpower|e] dies from combat.

name: Morale Damage Taken
description: This impacts the amount of damage to [morale|e] a unit takes in [combat|e].

name: Strength Damage Done
description: This impacts the amount of damage dealt to an enemy. For [ships|e], this damages the actual [ship|e], while for [regiments|e] this determines how much [manpower|e] they will kill.

name: Morale Damage Done
description: This impacts the amount of damage dealt to the [morale|e] of an enemy in [combat|e].

name: Discipline
description: This impacts both the damage that a [regiment|e] does in [combat|e] and the [damage_taken|e]. The higher the discipline the more damage done, and the less [damage_taken|e].

name: Movement Speed
description: This value determines how fast a [unit|e] moves across the map.

name: Military Tactics
description: This reduces the [damage_taken|e] of a [regiment|e] in [combat|e].

name: Combined Arms
description:
[armies] and [navies] with balanced compositions of [unit_categories|e] receive a bonus to their [combat_power|e] in [battle|e] for each additional category involved. The strenght of the bonus may vary depending on technology and other sources.

In order to benefit from the Combined Arms bonus, an [army] cannot have #W 50%#! or more [regiments|e] of the same category. Examples of different [unit_categories|e] are [ShowUnitCategoryName('navy_light_ship')] and [ShowUnitCategoryName('navy_heavy_ship')], or [ShowUnitCategoryName('army_light_infantry')] and [ShowUnitCategoryName('army_heavy_cavalry')].

name: Average Morale
description: This is the average [morale|e] of all [regiments|e] or [ships|e] in a [unit|e].

name: Merchant
description: Merchants are a company loyal to a [country|e] that are present in a [market|e] and can use their [merchant_power|e] and [merchant_capacity|e] to [trade|e] [goods|e] with another [market|e] in the hope of a profit.

name: Subject Loyalty
description:
Every [subject|e] has a Subject Loyalty towards their [overlord|e]. Ranging from 0 to 100, once it drops below 50 the [subject] will become a [disloyal_subject|e].

Its value is directly impacted by [liberty_desire|e], and can be further decreased with the [ShowCabinetActionName('sow_disloyalty')] [cabinet_action|e].

name: Subject Territory Connectivity
description:
Subject Territory Connectivity measures how well connected a [subject|e]'s territory is to its [overlord|e], scored from 0 to 100.

A land connection starts at 100 and loses points for each area traversed based on how low its average [control|e] is. Areas with full control cost nothing; areas with no control reduce the score by up to 20 per area.

A maritime connection is scored from three components: the [maritime_presence|e] at the subject's exit port, the naval distance between the ports, and the [maritime_presence|e] at the overlord's arrival port. [subject_type|e] can increase or reduce the tolerated path distance.

No connection scores 0.

Higher connectivity increases its [subject_loyalty|e].

name: Subject Type
description:
Every [subject|e] has a Subject Type, which essentially outlines the rules that it must follow in regard to aspects like [war|e] and [heir_selection|e].

Subject Types also dictate the [subject_taxation|e] and [great_power_score|e] that each [subject] must surrender to its [overlord|e].

name: Subject Taxation
description: Subject Taxation is the [gold|e] that an [overlord|e] receives from their [subjects|e]. The exact amount is based on the Economy of the [subject], and is then scaled by the rules in the [subject_type|e].

name: Subject
description:
A Subject is any [country|e] that is subordinate to an [overlord|E].

It typically has limitations on its [diplomacy|e] in return for protection in a [war|e].

Subjects may also suffer [subject_taxation|e], and have a certain percentage of their [great_power_score|e] exacted by their [overlord]. Additionally, a subject may not become a [great_power|e]. The exact rules are dependent on the [subject_type|e].

Subjects have [subject_loyalty|e] towards their [overlord], and a [liberty_desire|e] - both of which indicate their current stance on their subordination, for example whether they are [loyal_subjects_short|e] or [disloyal_subjects_short|e].

Any subject may in turn be the [overlord] of other [countries], allowing long chains of Subject-[overlord] relationships.

Some subjects are [non_sovereign_subjects|e].

name: Non-Sovereign Subject
description: A Non-Sovereign Subject is a type of [subject|e] that cannot act independently of its [overlord|e] and thus has limited capacity to conduct [diplomacy|e] and cannot fight [wars|e] independently.

name: Overlord
description:
An Overlord is a [country|e] that has any number of [subjects|E] as its subordinates.

In return for protecting each [subject] in [wars|e], it typically receives [subject_taxation|e], and exacts a certain percentage of the [subject]'s [great_power_score|e]. The exact rules are dependent on each [subject]'s [subject_type|e].

Any Overlord may in turn be the [subject] of other [countries], allowing long chains of [subject]-Overlord relationships.

name: Ability
description:
Ability represents the different aptitudes of each [character|e]. The values of each range from 0 to 100. Newborn children start at 0 and gradually increase their Abilities as they grow up.

There are three types of Ability:
 - [adm_short|e]
 - [dip_short|e]
 - [mil_short|e]

Added together, they constitute the [character]'s [total_ability|e].

name: Societal Value
description:
$game_concept_societal_value_upper_desc$

[ShowDatabase('societal_values')]

name: Religious Head
description: It is the [character|e] considered to be in charge, and representative of, a whole [religion|e] denomination.

name: Excommunication
description:
Excommunication is an international status of a [ruler|e] with a severe religious and diplomatic penalty. All [countries|e] of the same [religion|e] gain [ShowBiasValue('opinion_excommunicated')|+=0] [opinion|e] of the excommunicated [country], and the [ShowCasusBelliName('cb_excommunication')] [casus_belli|e] against it. Atop of this, the excommunicated [country] receives the following penalties until their next ruler:
[ShowModifierEffect('excommunicated')]

name: Karma
description:
Karma is measured on a scale from #R -100#! to #R +100#!, and reflects the past deeds of a [country|e].
A country will benefit the most when its karma is in balance, between #G -33#! and #G +33#!.

name: Purity
description: It is the indication of how pure our [country|e] is according to [ShowReligionName('shinto')]. Purity is lost by contact with anything impure, such as killing and losing [people|e] in [battles|e], or epidemics, as death and blood are impure. It is gained through performing religious acts, such as pilgrimages to [holy_sites|e] or ritual suicide.

name: Honor
description:
How honorable our [country|e] is in the eyes of our people.

Maintaining the [purity|E] of our country above 75 will increase our [honor|E] while having low Purity will decrease it.
