Other religious and diplomatic actions may also affect it.

name: Yanantin
description: Yanantin represents the balance between two complementary but opposing entities. Following the mindset of the [ShowCultureGroupName('andean_group')] [cultures|e], harmony can only be achieved when a being, a man, darkness, the Sun, finds its complement and joins it, a woman, light, the Moon.

name: Righteousness
description: Righteousness is a measure of how the government is perceived to be following the philosophy and morals of $SECT_CONFUCIANISM_NAME$.

name: Harmony
description: Harmony is a measure of how well the [country|e] is following the principles of the Dào, having to balance between being influenced by [GetAutoModifier('negative_harmony').GetNameWithTooltip] or [GetAutoModifier('positive_harmony').GetNameWithTooltip]. The country will get many effects nudging it towards one or the other, mainly through [events|e], and should try to keep [GetAutoModifier('balanced_harmony').GetNameWithTooltip].

name: Self Control
description:
Self Control is a measure of how a [country|e] and its [ruler|e] are renouncing pleasures and material possessions, and how they follow the path of Yoga.

Having a positive value of $self_control$ will mean that they tend to asceticism, giving benefits to [stability|e], [migration|e], [annexation|e], and reduced [food_consumption|e], while having a negative $self_control$ means that they are tending towards depravity, giving increased [tax|e] and [food_consumption|e] but reduced [war_exhaustion|e]. Having $self_control$ balanced gives in turn better [research|e] speed, [prestige|e], and [estate_satisfaction|e].

name: Doom
description:
Doom is a special currency used by [countries|e] with the [ShowReligionAdjective('nahuatl')] [religion|e].

Owning [locations|e]—especially [towns_and_cities|e]—passively increases Doom.

Having a high Doom value decreases [ShowModifierTypeName('subject_loyalty')] and [ShowModifierTypeName('global_estate_target_satisfaction')] but increases [ShowModifierTypeName('stability_decay')].

There are a number of ways that decrease Doom, including:
- Killing [enemy|e] troops in [combat|e]
- Looting [locations] with high [development|e]

When the maximum Doom is finally reached, the [ruler|e] and their entire [dynasty|e] are sacrificed, and replaced with a new [ruler].

name: Religious Reform
description: A Religious Reform is sometimes required or embraced for the best outcome of a [religion|e], representing the constant adaptation of the rites and faith due to the desires of its believers and institutions.

name: Patriarch
description: Patriarchs are the highest-ranking bishops in certain [ShowReligionGroupAdjective('christian')] [religions|e]. There can be more than one of them in each [religion], ruling over their own patriarchate.

name: Religious Influence
description: It is a value of the ability that a [country|e] has to interact with and influence matters of its [primary_religion|e]. Depending on the [religion|e], the uses it will have will be different, as well as the ways for a [country] to acquire it.

name: Papal Bull
description: A Papal Bull is an international edict, enacted with [gold|e], which affects all [countries|e] of the [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] [religion|e]. While some Papal Bulls have [effects|e] and an enacted [law|e], all Papal Bulls have [modifiers|e] for the countries which scale in their effectiveness with the [papal_authority|e].

name: Papal Authority
description:
Papal Authority is a measure of how respected and acknowledged the [pope|e] is. It is an [international_organization_variable|e] of the [GetInternationalOrganizationType('catholic_church').GetName], with monthly changes driven by: [reform_desire|e], internal peace, doctrines, [cardinals|e], [excommunications|e], and other factors.
$PA_TOOLTIP_THRESHOLDS$

name: Religious War
description: A religious war is declared by an [international_organization|e] of countries of the same faith to a [heathen|e] country. The most prominent examples in the game are the #Y Crusades#! and #Y Jihads#! of the [ShowReligionGroupAdjective('christian')] and [ShowReligionGroupAdjective('muslim')] [religions|e].

name: Religious School
description:
The Holy Scripture may be infallible, but distinct schools of thought have developed on how laws and norms are best aligned with it.
Which school a [country|e] follows will affect its path ahead.

name: Religious Faction
description: They are different organizations inside a single [religion|e], representing different currents of thought inside it. They will try to vie among each other for the [country|e]'s patronage, and the [country] itself can interact with them and obtain different benefits.

name: Religious Focus
description: Some [religions|e] have attributes that a [country|e] can focus on to gain extra benefits. Once enough focuses have been completed, the [religion] can reform.

name: Religious Aspect
description: Some [religions|e] have aspects that further specialize the details of each [country_s|e] version of the [religion|e].

name: Urban Location
description:
This is a [location|e] with a significant human settlement. It can contain more specialized [buildings|e], and allows for the flourishing of [ShowPopTypeName('burghers')]. It is the opposite of a [rural_location|e].

Depending on its size, an [urban_location] can be a [ShowLocationRankName('town')], a [ShowLocationRankName('city')], or a [ShowLocationRankName('megalopolis')].

name: Rural Location
description: A [location|e] without a significant settlement, and therefore fewer opportunities to build special [buildings|e]. It is the opposite of [town_or_city|e].

name: Urban Rights
description:
Urban Rights are special privileges that a [country|e] can grant to a [town_or_city|e]. These can impact the [location|e] and/or the [country|e].

Some [countries] start with access to historical Urban Rights, and a number of them are granted from 1337. Later on, starting in the [ShowAgeName('age_3_discovery')], all [countries] can research the [advance_icon][ShowAdvanceName('town_rights_enable')] [advance|e], giving access to Urban Rights that allow for the specialization of [urban_locations|e] in a particular purpose, like producing a specific [good|e].

By default, a [ShowLocationRankName('town')] can have 1 Urban Right, a [ShowLocationRankName('city')] can have 2, and a [ShowLocationRankName('megalopolis')] can have 3, although some [government_reforms|e] can increase these values.

name: Location Rank
description:
Each [location|e] has a rank, which can be described as an [urban_location|e] or a [rural_location|e].

[ShowDatabaseWithIcon('location_rank')]

name: Corridor
description: Corridors are special [locations|e] that cannot be inhabited or [owned|e] by any [country|e], but, contrary to [wastelands|e], still can be traversed by [armies|e].

name: Strait
description: A Strait connects two [locations|e] that are separated by a [seazone|e], but are close enough to each other so [armies|e] can cross it without the need of a [navy|e].

name: K'atun
description:
A K'atun is a measure of time of the [ShowReligionAdjective('mayan')] people, it corresponds to 19.7 years. The end of one K'atun and start of a new one was marked by many ceremonies and festivities, making the occasion a truly important date for rulers and their people.

If by the time the current K'atun ends we have invested enough resources to prepare for the celebrations, we will gain [ShowModifier('katun_celebration')] for 10 years. On the other hand, if we are not ready we might gain [ShowModifier('katun_celebration_bad')] for 10 years. We will be fully ready once our [religious_influence|e] is at least 90.

name: Curia Action
description:
These are actions taken by the [curia|e] affecting the whole [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] world. Any [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] [country|e] is able to propose a debate to the [curia], and every [country] with a [cardinal|e] will be able to influence the outcome of the debate by either supporting or opposing it.

If passed, the effects will depend on which Curia Action was taken, but will apply to all [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] [countries].

name: Resolution
description:
These are actions taken by [international_organizations|e] affecting the whole organization. Any [member|e] [country|e] is able to propose a resolution to the other [members], and every [member] will be able to influence the outcome of the debate by either supporting or opposing it.

If passed, the effects will depend on which resolution was taken.

name: Cardinal
description:
A Cardinal is a representative of the [ShowReligionAdjective('catholic')] Church, just immediately behind the [pope]. Cardinals are assigned to [locations|e] via the construction of a special [building|e] called [ShowBuildingTypeName('seat_of_cardinal')], and they will be loyal to the [country|e] that [owns|e] that [location].

A [country] may use its Cardinals to participate in [curia_actions|e].

name: Canonization
description: A former [ruler|e] of a [country|e] can be canonized, that is, made into a [saint|e]. This will please the [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')] and instantly confer [legitimacy|e] and [prestige|e] upon the [country], scaled according to how able the [character|e] was when they were alive.

name: Maritime Presence
description:
The Maritime Presence we have along our coasts is vital both for [trade|e] and for our [control|e] over our territory.

Maritime Presence builds up over time, if we are at peace, just from having [ports|e], while a [blockade|e] will quickly reduce our presence. A [navy|e] in a [seazone|e] can quickly build up the presence again.

High $game_concept_maritime_presence$ reduces the [proximity|e] that is lost between [seazones|e] when calculating $game_concept_control$. $game_concept_maritime_presence$ in the coastal $game_concept_seazones$ of a [market|e] is also an important source of [merchant_power|e].

name: Maritime $game_concept_merchant_power$
description: Your $game_concept_merchant_maritime_power$ represents the ability of your [navies|e] to effectively protect and influence seaborne trade. It determines the amount of [merchant_power|e] that a [country|e] generates from having [maritime_presence|e] in the coastal [seazones|e] of a [market|e].

name: Blockade
description:
A blockade is when a [hostile|e] [navy|e] is present in the [seazone|e] outside a [port|e], the amount of [ships|e] needed depends on the [population|e] and [development|e] of the [ports|e] affected.

The most important effects of blockade:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Reduce [food|e] Production
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Reduce [maritime_presence|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Reduce [development]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Reduce [control|e]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$Reduce [prosperity|e]

name: Seazone
description: A seazone is similar to a [location|e] except that it only contains water. It is a division of the map that is not [owned|e] or [controlled|e] by anyone. If a seazone is coastal, it will also have [maritime_presence|e] from adjacent [countries|e].

name: Lake
description: Lakes represent inland bodies of water without any contact with the open sea except through possible rivers, so no [ships|e] of relevance are able to sail in them.

name: Sea Current
description: A $game_concept_sea_current$ is a particularity of certain [seazones|e] that allows for faster movement of [navies|e] in a specific direction.

name: Embarking
description: An [army|e] that is being transported by a [navy|e] can disembark from a [seazone|e] to an adjacent [coastal|e] [location|e].

name: Frozen Over
description: A frozen [seazone|e] can be traversed by [armies|e] and allows greater control over the lands it reaches; however, it will cause [navies|e] to get stuck until it thaws. Be careful when the weather changes, it can thaw with catastrophic consequences if an [army|e] is on the ice.

name: Impassable
description: This is a [location|e] or a [seazone|e] that can not be entered by [units|e], nor can anyone live there in any sustainable numbers.

name: Religious Unity
description: Religious unity is the percentage of the [country|e]'s [population|e] that follows the official state [religion|e].

name: Cultural Unity
description: Cultural unity is the percentage of the [country|e]'s [population|e] that is of the [primary_culture|e].

name: Liberty Desire
description:
Liberty Desire represents a [subject|e]'s current drive for independence from its [overlord|e], and it affects [subject_loyalty|e].

Its value is from -100 to +100, but it has a monthly decay towards 0.

The value is also used as a currency in some Subject Interactions.

name: Market Access
description:
Market Access represents how easily a [location|e] can interact with its [market|e], and depends on the distance to the [market_center|e].

Market Access is important in three key ways:

$BULLET$Locations will have higher [market_attraction_with_icon|e] towards [markets] with higher access. That means that [locations] will tend to belong to the closest [market].

$BULLET$[locations] in a [market] buy [goods_with_icon|e] and [food_with_icon|e] in order of their Market Access.

$BULLET$Low Market Access harms local industry by reducing the [output|e] of [buildings_with_icon|e], and the profit of [rgo_with_icon|e]

Market Access propagates better over seas and [rivers|e], and can be improved by constructing [roads|e] and $naval_category$, or by creating a new [market].

name: Sell Price
description:
The price at which [goods|e] are sold in a [location|e].
The Sell Price can be lower than the [market_price|e] if there is low [market_access|e].

name: Building Category
description: [building_types|e] are grouped in different Categories, which is primarily to identify which ones are similar.

name: Political Power
description:
Political Power is the clout that [pops|e] have in the sphere of [government|e]. It is used to calculate [estate_power|e] and [language_power|e], as well as the [dominant_upper_class_culture|e] of each [country|e].

Each [pop] exerts a different amount of Political Power dependent on the [estate|e] they belong to. For example, a Pop belonging to the [ShowEstateTypeName('nobles_estate')] naturally exerts hundreds of times more Political Power than a Pop belonging to the [ShowEstateTypeName('peasants_estate')].

name: Child Education
description:
[children|e] can be given an education from the age of #Y 3#!. This will determine how their [abilities|e] improve over time.

Every month a [child] has a [GetDefine('NCharacter','MONTHLY_STAT_INCREASE_CHANCE_FOR_CHILD')|Y]% chance to increase their [abilities] according to their education.

name: Exploration
description:
An exploration is a mission led by an [explorer|e] with the intention of [discovering|e] an uncharted [area|e] of land or sea within [naval_range|e].

Every exploration has a progress cost, increased by the distance from [capital|e], but reduced by [naval_range|e]. The speed at which an [explorer] works through this progress is dependent on their [mil|e].

Each exploration has a monthly [gold|e] cost, which an [explorer] will reduce proportionately to their [adm|e].

Once the exploration reaches the end of its [exploration_progress|e], the [area] will be [discovered], and the [explorer] will return.

name: Exploration Progress
description: Each [area|e] has a cost to be fulfilled before it is fully [explored|e]. This depends on a lot of factors, but primarily on the skill of the [explorer|e].

name: Known World
description: This is the portion of the World that you have currently [discovered|e]. Any territory not discovered by your [country|e] is considered [terra_incognita|e].

name: Terra Incognita
description: Before a [location|e] has been [discovered|e] by a [country|e] through an [exploration|e] or other sources, it is not visible on the map, nor can it be interacted with by that country, and is referred to as Terra Incognita, Latin for unknown land.

name: Discover
description: When a [location|e] is discovered, the [terra_incognita|e] is removed from it, and is now visible and interactable with.

name: Explorer
description: An explorer is a [character|e] who has certain [traits|e] which are useful when they are assigned on an [exploration|e].

name: Conquistador
description: A $game_concept_conquistador$ is a [character|e] who has been assigned the task to conquer a foreign land and create a new [subject|e] of our [country|e].

name: Immortality
description: When a [character|e] is immortal, they will not die from old age. They are however still susceptible to death from other worldly causes, such as [battle|e] or something far worse, like [disease|e].

name: Balance
description: The monthly Balance is based on the total amount of [incomes|e] and [expenses|e] that a [country|e] has. The result impacts the country's [treasury|e].

name: Treasury
description: This is the amount of [gold|e] a [country|e] has. If it goes negative, a [loan|e] will automatically be taken. If no more [loans] can be taken, the country will go [bankrupt|e].

name: Income
description: This is the [gold|e] that a [country|e] gets each month. It includes [taxes|e] from each [estate|e] and income from [trades|e].

name: Expense
description: These are the running costs of a country. This includes paying for [armies|e], [navies|e], [trades|e], [artists|e], [fortifications|e], [colonial_charters|e], and more each month.

name: GDP per capita
description: The Gross Domestic Product per capita is the total [income|e] of a [country|e] divied by its total [population|e].

name: Cost of the Court
description: The court is the extended household of the [ruler|e], including all those who regularly attend on them. In the largest courts, this number can grow to many thousands, comprised of camarilla, household staff, clergy, gentry, bodyguards, harem, concubines, eunuchs, and many more roles. All these people do not come for free, and this figure represents the cost of having them around.

name: Diplomatic Spending
description:
Should we ever need it, the amount of [diplomats_with_icon|e] and [diplomatic_capacity_with_icon|e] at our disposal can be increased by spending extra [gold|e].

Diplomatic Spending also improves [subject_loyalty_with_icon|e].

name: Maintenance
description: Each month we will need to pay [army_maintenance|e] for our [regiments|e] and [navy_maintenance|e] for our [ships|e].

name: Army Maintenance
description: We need to pay, equip, feed, and clothe our [armies|e], or they will not be very effective. Army Maintenance is a way of measuring how many [gold|e] we are diverting towards making sure our [armies] have everything they need. Without this, [morale|e] will suffer, and our troops will be less effective.

name: Navy Maintenance
description:
It is lovely when we have a grand, shiny fleet of [ships|e] ready to set sail. These vessels do not just maintain themselves, though: [gold|e] must be spent on keeping them shipshape. Navy Maintenance is a way of measuring how many resources we are diverting towards keeping our ships in good condition.

At lower maintenance, [morale|e] will suffer, and our ships will be less effective, both in combat and at increasing [maritime_presence|e].

name: Fort Maintenance
description: [forts|e] are useful for repelling invading [armies|e], but they use [gold|e] in upkeep to make sure they are capable of doing their job. Fort Maintenance is a measure of how many resources a [country|e] is diverting towards ensuring their [forts|e] are in good shape. The more resources spent, the more effective the forts will be.

name: Bureaucracy Maintenance
description: This refers to the cost of running the [bureaucracy|e] reach month. A fully funded $game_concept_bureaucracy$ will have no negative modifiers, while a poorly funded will only have negatives.

name: Investing in Culture
description: This money is spent on [artists|e], so that they can create better [work_of_art|e]. It also directly increases the [prestige|e] of our [country|e].

name: Cost of Colonies
description: It costs [gold|e] to send ships, people, and supplies to maintain a [colonial_charter|e]. This cost is represented here.

name: Mercenary Income
description: This is the [gold|e] we get from renting our [armies|e] or [navies|e] as [mercenaries|e] to other [countries|e].

name: Hiring Mercenaries
description: This is our cost from hiring [mercenaries|e] to fight for us.

name: Building Subsidies
description: Some [buildings|e] may not be profitable, but we need the [goods|e] they produce for other reasons. Those buildings can be given a [subsidy|e].

name: Subsidy
description: When a [building|e] is not profitable, it will not buy the [goods|e] it needs, and will not function. A [country|e] can elect to subsidy a [building], paying it enough [gold|e] each month to survive.

name: Exploration Cost
description: [exploration|e] missions have a maintenance cost that can be reduced by some [advances|e], [laws|e], and [privileges|e], as well as by the [explorer|e]'s [adm|e] ability.

name: Diplomatic Expense
description: Whether by [treaty|e] or by force, this is the amount being extracted from our [treasury|e] by other [countries|e].

name: Diplomatic Income
description: This is the amount entering our [treasury|e] from other [countries|e], whether they like it or not.

name: Stability Investment
description: Spending part of the [budget|e] on [stability|e] is one of three main ways to increase stability, the others involve using a [cabinet_actions|e] on it or having enough [ShowEstateTypeName('clergy_estate')] of the [primary_religion|e].

name: Sound Toll
description:
There are some straits in the world where the controller can exact a fee from [trades|e] traveling past it. For example:
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowLocationName('oresund')]
$BULLET_WITH_TAB$[ShowLocationName('gulf_izmit')]

Each Sound Toll is linked to a specific land [location|e] you need to own in order to be the controller of the strait, and the [income|e] generated from the toll is scaled by your [control|e] in that [location].

name: Trade Profit
description: The profit of trade primarily depends on the difference between the [market_prices|e] of the [goods|e] in the [export_market|e] and the [import_market|e]. There is also a maintenance cost that will reduce the profit, and some trades may be forced to pay a [sound_toll|e].

name: Great Power $game_concept_great_power_score_short$
description:
Great Power Score is the indisputable measure of which [country|e] is the best. The top highest scoring $game_concept_countries$ are the [great_powers|e]. The total number of Great Powers varies depending on the Score of the top Great Power compared with the rest.

$game_concept_countries$ earn $game_concept_great_power_score_short$ by owning more [population|e], having higher [prestige|e], increasing [country_rank|e], and various other sources.

[subjects|e] also forfeit a certain percentage of their Score to their [overlord|e], depending on their [subject_type|e].

name: Great Power $game_concept_great_power_points_short$
description:
Great Power Points measure how much of the world's economic territory a [country|e] dominates. A [country] earns points by controlling at least two-thirds of the ownable [locations|e] in an [area|e], counting [subjects|e] at a reduced rate. Each area is worth 1-10 points based on its potential tax base relative to the world median.

Accumulate enough points to become a [regional_power|e] or [great_power|e].

name: Great Power $game_concept_great_power_rank_short$
description: Great Power Rank shows the current position a [country|e] holds in the race for final victory. The Rank is decided by the sum of the [great_power_score|e].

name: Event
description:
Events are occurrences which happen to a [country|e] throughout the game if the conditions for them are met. They usually have an [effect|e] attached to them and tell a piece of ingame narrative.
Some [countries] have access to [dynamic_historical_events|e].

name: Dynamic Historical Event
description: These are historical [events|e] that will happen to a specific [country|e] within a specified time period if the conditions are right for it.

name: Event Option
description: Every [event|e] has at least one option that the player can choose. If the event is a [dynamic_historical_event|e], it may have a [historical_option|e].

name: Historical Option
description: This is a historical [event|e], and this [event_option|e] is the one that will make you take the same decision as the [country|e] did in history.

name: Mission
description: Missions are packages of individual [tasks|e] which are available to a [country|e]. They serve as a guidance for the [country] and grant useful rewards after finishing a task or all the tasks, depending on the settings.

name: Mission Task
description: A task is a sub-element of a [mission|e]. They are made of a requirement and can contain a reward if the aforementioned condition is fulfilled. All tasks have to be completed in order to finish a [mission].

name: Minting
description: Minting is a way to increase our [treasury|e] at the cost of [inflation|e]. If we do not mint any coins, our [inflation] may decrease.

name: Coastal
description: A [location|e] that is coastal is in contact with a [seazone|e], and as such will have a [port|e] and will be able to build [ships|e] if it has the appropriate [building|e], such as a [ShowBuildingTypeName('wharf')] or a [ShowBuildingTypeName('dock')].

name: Inland
description:
A [location|e] that is inland is not in contact with a [seazone|e], so it will not have a [port|e] and will not be able to build [ships|e].

The opposite of an inland $game_concept_location$ is a [coastal|e] $game_concept_location$.

name: Ducats
description:
Representing liquid wealth, it is the primary form of currency in every [country|e]. The amount of Ducats that a [country] currently owns is its [treasury|e].

Ducats can be generated through [taxes|e] from [estates|e] and [subjects|e], and are spent on almost everything, from constructing [buildings|e] to maintaining [armies|e]. They change hands through the purchase and sale of [food|e] and [goods|e], and can be invested into [stability|e] and the [court|e].

name: Hemisphere
description:
Every [location|e] lies in one of two Hemispheres: north or south of the equator.

The Hemisphere primarily determines the months in which [winter|e] is likely to occur: around January in the Northern Hemisphere, and around June in the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Winter
description:
Winter affects [locations|e] in negative ways. The way each winter happens is random, but its severity, or [winter_level|e], is influenced by the [climate|e].

The months that winter falls in depend on the [hemisphere|e] of the [location].

name: Winter Level
description:
Winter Level is the severity of [winter|e] in a [location|e]. Harsher [winter] will halt [constructions|e] and even [frozen_freeze_over|e] some shallow [seazones|e].

[armies|e] are unable to move into [locations] with [ShowTopographyName('mountains')] [topography|e] during Normal or Severe [winter].

[armies] sheltered in a friendly [fort|e] or within its [zone_of_control|e] do not suffer winter [attrition|e]. This shelter extends to forts owned by your direct [subjects|e] and to your direct [overlord|e].

The maximum Winter Level that a [location] can experience is dependent on the local [climate|e].

The Winter Levels are as follows:
- [ShowModifier('winter_none')]
- [ShowModifier('winter_mild')]
- [ShowModifier('winter_normal')]
- [ShowModifier('winter_severe')]

name: Improve Relations
description: It is an action of [diplomacy|e] with the intention of improving the [opinion|e] that another [country|e] has of our own [country].

name: Primary Religion Tolerance
description:
The $game_concept_primary_religion_tolerance$ represents how much a [country|e] favors the followers of its [primary_religion|e]. It impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of [pops|e] of the $game_concept_primary_religion$, and modifies a Country's [diplomatic_opinion|e] towards brethren $game_concept_countries$.

$game_concept_primary_religion_tolerance$ is generally positive by default, and can be increased even further by certain [laws|e], [privileges|e], and [societal_values|e].

name: Tolerance of Heretics
description:
The $game_concept_heretic_tolerance$ represents the social and political discrimination [heretics|e] suffer in a [country|e]. It impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of heretic [pops|e], and modifies a Country's [diplomatic_opinion|e] towards heretic $game_concept_countries$.

$game_concept_heretic_tolerance$ is generally low by default, and can be modified by certain [laws|e], [privileges|e], and [societal_values|e].

name: Tolerance of Heathens
description:
The $game_concept_heathenry_tolerance$ represents the social and political discrimination [heathens|e] suffer in a [country|e]. It impacts the [pop_satisfaction|e] of heathen [pops|e], and modifies a Country's [diplomatic_opinion|e] towards heathen $game_concept_countries$.

$game_concept_heathenry_tolerance$ is generally very low by default, and can be modified by certain [laws|e], [privileges|e], and [societal_values|e].

name: Autocephalous Patriarchate
description: An Autocephalous Patriarchate is a group of [countries|e] of the same eastern [ShowReligionGroupAdjective('christian')] [religion|e] that have as the head of their Church one bishop who does not answer to any other within the [religion]. The [international_organization_leader_short|e] of the Autocephalous Patriarchate is conferred extra benefits, and being a member can have benefits too, until the member [country] outgrows the [international_organization_leader_short], at which time it may be beneficial to branch out and create their own. If the patriarchate has a [holy_site|e] within it, then the seat of that patriarchate can be relocated there for extra benefits.

name: Sect
description: $sect_desc$

name: Hindu Branch
description: $hindu_branch_desc$

name: Heathen
description:
Any [religion|e] of a different [religion_group|e] than the [primary_religion|e] in a [country|e] will be considered heathen.

Depending on the [heathenry_tolerance|e] in a $game_concept_country$, heathen [pops|e] will generally have lower [pop_satisfaction|e], and conducting [diplomacy|e] with heathen $game_concept_countries$ may prove more difficult.

name: Heretic
description:
Any [religion|e] that shares [religion_group|e] with the [primary_religion|e] in a [country|e] will be considered heretical.

Depending on the [heretic_tolerance|e] in a $game_concept_country$, heretic [pops|e] will generally have lower [pop_satisfaction|e], and conducting [diplomacy|e] with heretic $game_concept_countries$ may prove more difficult.

name: Subsidization
description: Some production [buildings|e] may have their financial losses [subsidized|e] by their [owner|e]. Any [gold|e] losses that such a building may be incurring will be paid directly from the [country|e]'s [balance|e], allowing it to operate as normal.

name: River
description:
A [location|e] may have a River, a moving body of water.

Rivers are not navigable by [navies|e], but they impose a [crossing|e] combat malus on [armies|e] who attempt to enter a [location] with a River. Additionally, they slightly increase the [population_capacity|e] of a location.

name: Output
description: The amount of [goods|e] that is created either from a [building|e] as [produced_goods|e], or as [raw_materials|e] from a [location|e].

name: R.G.O.
description:
Initials of $game_concept_resource_gathering_operations$. Each [location|e] has a [raw_material|e] that is created from $rgo_mining$, $rgo_farming$, $rgo_gathering$, $rgo_forestry$, or $rgo_hunting$.

Each level of $game_concept_rgo$ can [employ|e] up to #V 1,000#! [rgo_pops|e], while the maximum level depends on [development|e], [advances|e], and other things.

name: Special Status
description: Members with a Special Status in an [international_organization|e] enjoy certain privileges or have certain duties to fulfill. In some cases, the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of the organization has a special status to emphasize their unique position. Other organizations have [electors|e] instead which are represented with a special status.

name: Special Status Power
description: This is the political power that a group of [members|e] with a specific [special_status|e] has in an [international_organization|e]. This influence can be relevant for passing certain [parliament_issues|e] in the [parliament|e] unless those are resolved via a [resolution|e].

name: International Organization Leader
description:
An [international_organization|e] may have a [country|e] as its [international_organization_leader_short|e]. Each [international_organization] is different, but in general, it is the most powerful [country|e] in the [international_organization].

Some organizations have a system to vote for the [country] that has to be the [international_organization_leader_short], while others rely on other systems to define their leadership, and others may have no [international_organization_leader_short] at all.

name: International Organization Value
description: Values in an [international_organization|e] can be used to represent different mechanics depending on the $game_concept_international_organization$. In some cases, it represents the authority of the [international_organization_leader_short|e] of the organization, like in the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetName] or the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('middle_kingdom').GetName]. In others, like the [GetInternationalOrganizationType('sect').GetName], it represents the influence of the $game_concept_international_organization$ itself. There may be other uses for the values, and it will depend on each $game_concept_international_organization$ type.

name: Land Ownership Rule
description: Some [international_organizations|e] are capable of owning [locations|e]. The $game_concept_land_ownership_rule$ describes the nature of this ownership, and what [modifiers|e] apply on these Locations.

name: Emperor
description: The Emperor is the [international_organization_leader_short] of the [holy_roman_empire|e]. It is the duty of the Emperor to protect the [members|e] from external and internal threats.

name: Imperial Law Level
description:
The law level describes how decentralized versus centralized the specific law for the [holy_roman_empire|e] is. A lower level represents higher power of the [hre_emperor|e] while a higher level represents a decentralized status.

Reforms can be only taken at their adjacent level, which means the Emperor cannot select a Level 2 reform if the current law is on a Level 4 reform. Most [laws|e] start at level #Y 3#!.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description:
The [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetName] is an [international_organization|e] which dominates the political sphere of [ShowRegionName('north_german_region')], [ShowRegionName('south_german_region')] and partially [ShowRegionName('italy_region')] and [ShowRegionName('france_region')]. The [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetNameWithNoTooltip] is an amalgamation of countless [countries|e] of insignificant to medium power who all fall under the protection of their [international_organization_leader_short|e].

The [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetLeaderTitle] is the head of this organization which gets elected into this position.

name: Electoral College
description:
The $game_concept_hre_electoral_college$ consists of the [ShowSpecialStatusNamePlural('elector')] of the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetName].

The law of the [ShowLawName('golden_bull')] influences the way [ShowSpecialStatusNamePluralWithNoTooltip('elector')] cast their vote due to the following factors:
- the influence of the [country_rank|e] is established
- the influence of [opinion|e] is halved
- the influence of the [great_power_score|e] is quadrupled

name: Imperial Circle
description: A regional grouping of [holy_roman_empire|e] members. The [hre_emperor|e] can target certain actions directly at an entire [imperial_circle|e] through the [circle_leader|e].

name: Circle Satisfaction
description: A measure of how content the members of an [imperial_circle|e] are with their [circle_leader|e]. Higher satisfaction rewards the [circle_leader] with [prestige|e] and [diplomatic_reputation|e].

name: Circle Leader
description: The country which has been designated as as the leader of a [imperial_circle|e]. The [circle_leader] acts as an intermediary between the members of their [imperial_circle] and the [hre_emperor|e].

name: Promote
description: [pops|e] will [promote|e] from [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')] when there are possible positions for them in their [location|e]. Pops need to belong to at least a [tolerated_culture|e] in order to promote.

name: Demote
description: [pops|e] will demote to [ShowPopTypeName('peasants')] when there are too many of their current [pop_type|e] in their [location|e].

name: Disease Resistance
description: This impacts how likely [pops|e] and [characters|e] are to survive [diseases|e], like the [ShowDiseaseName('bubonic_plague')].

name: Parliament
description:
A [country|e] can call its [estates|e] into a session of $game_concept_parliament$, to solve any [parliament_issue|e] they may have, while also giving the opportunities to create a [casus_belli|e], raise [taxes|e], increase [army_levies|e] and [navy_levies|e], or change any of the current [laws|e]. Any [estate|e] may have a [parliament_agenda|e] to resolve before they will pledge their support.

$game_concept_parliament$ may take place in the [capital|e] or another [location|e], as long as it's a city, town, or [province_capital|e], and has more than one [proximity|e], which receives some small benefits. If the [location] becomes [occupied|e], the $game_concept_parliament$ will fail.

[international_organizations|e] such as the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetName] can have a $game_concept_parliament$, too. However, the parliament system depends on the type of Organization as some require the support of [members|e] of a specific [special_status|e] and their [special_status_power|e] to pass.

name: Parliament Type
description:
A [parliament|e] can be a different [parliament_type]. This affects how the parliament functions.

[ShowParliamentTypes]

name: Parliament Agenda
description:
Any [estate|e] may have a $game_concept_parliament_agenda$ to resolve before they will pledge their support. This may be costly for the [country|e], as the support given relies on the [estate_power|e] the estate has.

In the context of [international_organizations|e], the [members|e] of a [special_status|e] will instead present their $game_concept_parliament_agenda$. Accepting those may either give their guaranteed support in form of their [special_status_power|e].

name: Parliament Issue
description:
This is something that has been under debate for a while, and will need to be resolved in [parliament|e] by the [estates|e] or the [country|e] will become weaker.

For [international_organizations|e], these debates need to be negotiated with the powerful [members|e] with a [special_status|e].

name: Parliament Requests
description: These are actions that a [country|e] can spend [parliament_support|e] on to get through.

name: Parliament Support
description: This is a value which represents how willing the [parliament|e] is in passing a [parliament_issue|e]. It is also required for when the state wants to perform a specific [parliament_request|e].

name: Parliament Base Support
description: This impacts the initial [parliament_support|e] when a [parliament|e] is called. It is increased mainly by [crown_power|e], but [laws|e], [government_reforms|e] and [advances|e] can also impact it.

name: Parliament Seat
description: This is the [location|e] where the [parliament|e] of a [country|e] or of an [international_organization|e] takes place.

name: Production Method
description: This is something that can be changed in a [building|e] to change the [goods|e] required for its performance and/or what the building itself is capable of doing.

name: Legislative Efficiency
description: This impacts how quickly a [country|e] can implement [laws|e], [government_reforms|e], and [estate_privileges|e].

name: Isolate
description: A [country|e] that is isolated will not allow any other country to [export|e] or [import|e] [goods|e] in their [markets|e]. They may give some countries exclusive rights to ignore these rules.

name: Score
description:
This is a way to track how well a [country|e] is performing. Each country is ranked in [adm_short|e], [dip_short|e], and [mil_short|e] performance, and gain score out of their rank there.
Larger countries also gain score from holding [victory_cards|e] which they get one each [age|e].

name: Victory Card
description: A Victory Card is a goal to conquer an entire [area|e] on the map for a [country|e]. When the entire area is [owned|e], [controlled|e], and a [core|e], the country will gain [score|e].

name: Map Mode Slot
description: A Map Mode Slot is a container with several map modes. Click the slot repeatedly to cycle through them. Open any map mode category and right click on any map mode to add it to a slot.

name: Legal Male
description: A Legally Male is a female [character|e] who is considered, by law, to be a man. This gives them the same rights as their male counterparts in the question of [heir_selection|e]. This status may be declared on a woman with the [ShowCharacterInteractionName('prefection')] [character_interaction|e].

name: Payment
description: This is an arrangement made in an [international_organization|e] where some members are obliged to pay other [members|e] [gold|e], [manpower|e], [sailors|e] or something else in return for their membership of the organization. Payments can be applied or repealed through different [laws|e].

name: Fog of War
description:
The shroud that obscures [discovered|e] parts of the map is called the [fow].

[units|e] belonging to other [countries|e] are [hidden|e] while they lurk in the [fow].

A [location|e] is always visible to its [controller|e]. Furthermore, a [country|e] can always see into [cores|e] that they [own|e], even if they are [occupied|e] by an [enemy|e].

[allies|e], [subjects|e], and [overlords|e] share their vision with each other.

Some [locations|e] will always be in the [fow], for example those with [ShowVegetationName('forest')] [vegetation|e] or [ShowTopographyName('mountains')] [topography|e].

[seazones|e] with the [ShowTopographyName('narrows')] [topography] will only obstruct vision from other [seazones].

name: Hidden
description:
A [unit|e] positioned inside the [fow|e] is [hidden] to other [countries|e].

When a [unit] is hidden, other [countries] will not even be aware of its existence, let alone have info on its composition.

Hidden [units] receive no direct [combat|e] bonus, but ambushes can often give a strategic edge.

name: Natural Harbor Suitability
description: How well the [location|e] naturally lends itself to the docking of ships and loading/unloading of men and material, before any man-made improvements. It makes port [buildings|e] cheaper to construct, and improves [harbor_capacity|e].

name: Harbor Capacity
description:
Harbor Capacity reduces the cost of going from sea to land and vice versa in the [proximity|e] and [trade|e] calculations.

The Harbor Capacity of a [location] depends mainly on its [natural_harbor_suitability|e], but many port-related [buildings|e] can also increase it greatly.

name: Location Importance
description: This is determined based on a multitude of factors such as the [location|e]'s harbor suitability, its [population|e] size, how many [roads|e] lead to it, how many [buildings|e] it has, whether or not it is our [capital|e], if it has a [ShowBuildingTypeName('castle')], as well as its [market_access|e].

name: Monthly Trade & Tax Income
description: This is the monthly [income|e] from [trading|e] and [taxes|e] combined.

name: Monthly Manpower
description: This is the monthly gain of new [manpower|e] for the [country|e].

name: Coalition
description: [countries|e] whose [antagonism|e] towards a particular [country|e] has exceeded acceptable bounds may decide to join a Coalition targeting that country. To join, a country requires [antagonism|e] above 50 and [opinion|e] below −50 towards the target, must be within diplomatic range, and cannot be at war, in a truce, or in a union with the target — nor a subject of the target (tributaries excepted). Members will defend each other if the target attacks one of them, and may collectively declare [war|e] on the target. A member cannot leave while at war with the target, but will automatically depart if their [antagonism|e] falls below 30 while at peace with the target. A Coalition dissolves immediately if its leader leaves, or if the target country ceases to exist.

name: Revolutionary
description: The [revolution] is a unique transformation of the society of a [country|e] during the [ShowAgeName('age_6_revolutions')]. States which go through the [ShowDisasterName('revolution_disaster')] and fail to defend their absolute state might become [revolutionary], granting them access to powerful [actions|e], [reforms|e] and [laws|e] at the cost of becoming a potential target of non-[revolutionary] states.

name: Revolutionary Target
description: This is the beating heart of the Revolution and the most powerful [revolutionary|e] [country|e].

name: Celestial Authority
description: This is the measure of the legitimacy of the leader of the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('middle_kingdom').GetName]. It is used to pass [laws|e] and [policies|e] within that [international_organization|e].

name: Share of Power
description:
This is the measure of strength of a particular opposing side during the [ShowSituationName('fall_of_delhi')] [situation|e]. [GetCountry('DLH').GetName] can increase it through the following means:
- Situation Actions
- [events|e]
- Special Peace Treaties
- Diplomatic Support from other [countries|e]

Opposers can increase theirs through offensive wars and victories against [GetCountry('DLH').GetNameWithNoTooltip].

name: Entrenchment
description:
This is how embedded into [government|e] a [bureaucracy|e] is. The higher the Entrenchment, the more it does, the more it costs, and the harder it is to get rid of.

It also impacts the [estate_satisfaction] of [estates|e] that like or dislike the $game_concept_bureaucracy$ in question.

name: Movement Type
description: A Movement encapsulates ideas moving through a population. This can have various effects on each [pop|e] it touches.

name: Movement
description: A Movement is when a new [movement_definition|e] breaks out in a [location|e]. These serve as epicenters for each [movement_definition].

name: Divorce
description: A way to end up a [marriage|e], often requires permission from a third party.

name: Country Personality
description:
$game_concept_ai_personality_upper_desc$
[ShowDatabase('ai_personality')]

name: Country Disposition
description:
$game_concept_ai_disposition_upper_desc$
[ShowValues('ai_disposition')]

name: Pentarchy
description: The Pentarchy represents the traditional seats of power of [ShowReligionName('orthodox')]. Each of the [locations|e] that serve as a seat of the Pentarchy will give a different [modifier|e] to the [country|e] that owns it, and once a [country] owns all five seats those [modifiers] will be doubled.

name: Chivalric Order
description: A #Y Chivalric Order#! is an exclusive brotherhood of noble warriors dedicated to a country's martial ideals. Eligible characters may be invited to join, receiving the order's character modifiers and bonuses. The country itself gains the order's country modifiers as long as it has an active order and a ruler who is a member.
